title: I like you
body:
As appropriate between old friends as new lovers, warmth, affection and genuine joy in the company of another is expressed by the giving of #1 a gift hovering between friendship and the possibility of something more.

Those wishing to reciprocate the feelings expressed may do so with an excited #157, a disingenuous #163, an anticipatory (if not presumptive) #61 or #124, a playful #170, #86 or #148, a passionate if potentially overenthusiastic #59, or a non-committal #105. Receivers wishing to advise caution may do so with #11, #49, or #65, while those unable for some reason to accept the proffered sentiment can express regret or longing with #17 or #95. Repudiation with explanation is offered through #104, #103, or #63; simple and potentially cruel dismissal can be given with #193, #8, #184, #101 and an unequivocal #181.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: April 2013 book layout text differs (similarity 0.931; mainly layout trims/reference formatting).

title: How you doin'?
body:
A cheeky, non-committal edge makes #3 an excellent opening gambit. Whilst possible to send such a message in the context of a long-held friendship, or the first flush of enthusiasm for the company of a newfound comrade, such an implicitly flattering gesture is rarely entirely lacking in romantic subtext.

Responses can vary from the enthusiastically romantic #13, #59, to the direct #5, playful #56 or dismissive #122 or #147. Receivers unconvinced of their own worth may employ #38, while for those confused by the Bearer’s advances, or unsure of their identity, #12 or #35 may provide means of clarification. Should romantic intent be clear and a Receiver unwilling or unable to respond in kind, #17, #104 or #95 may provide appropriate and (in some cases) complimentary means of refusal. Any offended by an anonymous donor can make their feelings clear with an emphatic #103, #111 or #98, although such reactions are somewhat unlikely to give the Bearer much encouragement.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Shall we?" (5.1)

title: Only you
body:
This Bearer may be confused, or unsure of their path or even their desires, but their one certainty is the Receiver. Particularly powerful should the Bearer’s changing circumstances or the Receiver’s worries appear to be threatening their intimacy, or worse, preventing it from developing, #4 makes it clear that the Bearer, at least, has no intention of allowing such obstacles to interfere. Whether signifying craving for closeness, grateful recognition of continual support or simply reaffirmation of a significant bond, this is a passionate declaration: the Bearer’s world may be in turmoil, but the Receiver is a cornerstone.

Passionately romantic Receivers can use #46 or #66 to respond in kind, while #60 counters patience. Receivers unhappy with the strength of the Bearer’s feelings can indicate this with #49, while #154 and #22 make the lack of reciprocity explicit. Those repulsed by the Bearer’s declaration can use #74, #180, or #184 to make their feelings clear in no uncertain terms.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Nothing but you" (5.1)

title: Drink?
body:
A convivial drink is an excellent way to break all but the hardest of social ice, and this proposes just such an encounter. Whether an initial approach, an attempted conclusion to prolonged periods of ambiguous romantic tension, or when a relationship has broken and the Bearer wishes to repair it, this is as much a question as it is a laying of one's cards on the table.

Immediate acceptance can be signalled playfully with #105 or #124, simply with #73, or enthusiastically with #42 or #96. More time can be requested by those with positive intention with #83 or #60; conditions can be imposed with #94; #31 offers means of enquiring as to the Bearer’s situation or intent; and attempts at reconciliation can be accepted with #118. Receivers distinctly unimpressed with the suggestion can send #103 or #111, whereas those wishing to let the Bearer down gently have #67, #71, or #104 with which to do so.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Here goes nothing
body: Sincere and playful, this message suggests courage. A Bearer wishes to proceed with an enterprise or amorous venture they consider above their due. Receivers wishing to acquiesce with the Bearer’s assessment of their worth might reply with a #25 here; while those tentatively wishing to suggest further acquaintance may do so with a cautious #5 or direct #3. Any who’ve been awaiting just such contact can articulate this with #124. Receivers already devoted to the Bearer can say so with #46, those wishing to reflect the Bearer’s sentiment but unable to do so have #95; and any prevented by circumstance can use #17 or #60 to explain their situation.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: By way of introduction
body:
Congratulations, Receiver, the Bearer of #7 has been admiring you from afar, and wishes for the chance to become better acquainted. For Bearers, #7 is an excellent method of approaching a Receiver hitherto unintroduced who has caught one’s attention, or of inviting a casual associate to further intimacy.

Those wishing to convey enthusiastic assent can use a courteous #187, #124 or #5. Strictly platonic intent can be signalled with #154, whereas those intent on romance can use #13 or #3 to indicate the desire to take things further. Receivers unwilling to further acquaintance with the Bearer can repel their advances with a curt #103 or #48, a firm #104 or #181, a disparaging #169, #184 or #180, or a tactful #99, #188 or #186.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Laugh out loud
body:
Such a gift conveys shared joy and pleasure, grounded firmly in humour rather than romance. Beware, however; for Receivers with romantic intent may feel rebuked, merely clowns to the Bearer. Of course, for those not especially enamoured in the first place, or wishing to imply a Platonic yet sustained regard for the Receiver, this may be no bad thing.

Echoing the Bearer’s message reinforces the mutuality of such appreciation, while #121 and #151 express gratitude for the sentiment, #55 articulates the closeness between Bearer and Receiver, #80 playfully requests further detail, and #48 or #36 express disenchantment with the Bearer’s message.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Psst
body:
Something is barring smooth communication – an overbearing companion, a jealous rival, a busy workplace or simply a party where all tongues wag freely - and the Bearer has something interesting to communicate or some secret amusement to share. #9 suggests a private meeting, often short and impromptu, where parties involved can speak openly – generally, a whispered word or written card inform the Receiver of location and time. Various problems attend such a move – not only must Bearers come prepared, but the time-sensitive nature of the message can mean Receivers have no means of refusal but silence and absence. However, should such a gambit work, it is of the greatest convenience – and, possibly, romance.

Replying in equivalent terms is usually impractical, but should opportunity arise, #124 communicates emphatic acceptance, #87 willingness, #67 apologetic refusal, #143 or #80 enquiry, #42 excitement, #41 teasing dismissal, while #188, #193, #181 or #25 repel the invitation with admirable frankness.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Tread softly
body:
Both admission and warning, this speaks of hope and wary acceptance, albeit tempered with awareness of the fragility of happiness and the frailty of the human heart. This is a very private message; the Bearer may have not informed others of a delicate or troubling situation, and accordingly wish to avoid the vulnerability or possible humiliation of exposure. Still, a gift as intimate as this shows great faith in Receivers to respond with consideration, sensitivity and tact.

Sending #53, #4 or #57 in reply makes the Receiver’s commitment to the Bearer clear, whereas #12 or #80 asks for further information about their needs and #114 or #63 signal trouble ahead.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You intrigue me
body:
Confusion reigns, but never indifference. Perhaps the Bearer cannot discern the Receiver’s feelings, and seeks to know more; or perhaps genuine confusion about their motives and character provides occasion for the gift. Whatever the reason, this is never an admission of defeat, and requests the Receiver to be clear and forthright.

Reply in like form is rarely the end of the story, but Receivers can accept the Bearer’s confusion with #53 or an almost dismissive #117, indicate positive or romantic feelings with #59, articulate troubled or negative emotions with #69 or #146, tease with #173, promise for the future with #60, and make a potentially confusing situation clear with #154, #104 or a tempting #13.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "I just can't figure you out" (5.1, 5.4, 5.5, Code Generator)

title: Kiss me, you fool!
body:
Some Receivers just don’t take the hint. Kissing is often the first clear physical affirmation of affection or desire, and this Bearer wishes to hurry matters along somewhat. Unconcerned with plans for the future, echoes from the past, or the vagaries of the present, if the Receiver accepts, then the kiss is all that matters – for now.

Often a positive response in kind is redundant, although Receivers wishing to explore their feelings for the Bearer can always send #1, #34, #130 or #19 should they wish. Receivers unsure of the Bearer’s romantic situation can use #31 or #153 to make delicate enquiries, and a non-committal #105, #107 or #5 to invite further contact. #123 also rarely goes amiss in such situations. Should the Bearer’s identity be unknown, #12 and #35 request courteously that they make themselves known before the Receiver makes any decision, while #37, #103 and #104 repel their advances. #98 and #163 articulate confusion, feigned or otherwise, while Receivers fully cognizant of the Bearer’s identity can use #138, #74, #67, #180, #181 or even #186 or #169 to let them down with various degrees of directness.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Kiss me" (5.1)

title: I need a favour
body:
Whether the Bearer’s fondness for the Receiver is romantic, platonic, familial or noticeably ambiguous is irrelevant here – what marks this communication as important is the favour. It might be as simple and mundane as tracking down the Bearer’s lost cat, or as elaborate a scheme as posing as a paramour during an important social event. The task might seem odious, but it is surely somewhat uncivil to turn down a request so eloquently delivered. Furthermore, the Receiver will invariably be owed a favour in future, and favours can be an extremely valuable commodity.

Acceptance can be as basically expressed as #151 or #97; #70 or #87 imply enthusiasm; while #94 offers conditional acceptance and #101 frustration with a repeat offender. #125 is equivocal, while #80 requests further info and #55 assures the Bearer the Receiver will be there if needed. #30, on the other hand, makes the Receiver’s rejection quite clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Alas
body:
A plaintive admission of impossible attraction – a passing fancy, perhaps, or a longer infatuation – if not necessarily love. It is as much a compliment to the Receiver as it is a polite refusal, and an excellent way of letting another party down gently. Should the Bearer’s handicap be a third party, however, it is advisable to avoid their cognizance of such an exchange, lest wrath or worse should result.

Receivers minded to be kind may respond with a passionate #152, a regretful #53 or an affable #137; those wishing to take issue with the Bearer’s decision may challenge with a #87 or #41; while a wistful Receiver may wish simply to say #115. A playful #107 can also be sent, but it is advisable to consider #91 before doing so.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I trust you
body: A powerful mark of allegiance and bonding. Whether this trust relates to business, friendship, art, or love, there are few bolder ways to say it; the Bearer has faith in the Receiver to honour and protect them. Replying with #171 declares such conviction mutual, and #66 promises it lifelong; #46 and #47 are appropriate in cases of romantic devotion. A simple #121 expresses the Receiver’s gratitude for the Bearer’s faith. Receivers feeling themselves unworthy can say so with #38, and can suggest the Bearer’s possible foolishness with #131 or #26. Should they feel the Bearer’s trust overly long in coming, #124 and #20 say so with varying degrees of emphasis; #162 expresses satisfaction at the statement, and #157 joy. Receivers unwilling or unable to reciprocate, however, can say so with #54, or tease the Bearer with #163.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: April 2013 book layout text differs (similarity 0.96; mainly layout trims/reference formatting).

title: Obsession
body:
Sleepless nights, lost hours in reverie; desire run wild, and beyond the Bearer’s control. This Receiver simply will not leave the Bearer's head, welcome or otherwise. Whilst undeniably romantic, there is vulnerability and perhaps an edge of desperation in such an admission; attached is an implicit plea to spend more time together, so a Bearer thus stricken can cast aside their daydreams and focus on reality.

Passionate acceptance can be signalled with #46 or #66, while #65 or #49 advise caution, and #62 requests proof of such arrant devotion. Should the Bearer’s desires be unreciprocated, #104, #99, #154 or #22 all variously express and explain this, and #127 laments the awkwardness of the situation. A sarcastic #192 casts doubt on their genuineness. Meanwhile, those wishing to repudiate the Bearer’s gesture without sparing their feelings can employ a disbelieving #111 or #98, a dismissive #25 or an insulting #103 for the purpose.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Told you so
body:
Rarely a pleasant token to receive; often a satisfying one to give. A cheeky reminder that next time the Receiver might be well-served by listening to the Bearer, it is often rather left on desks or tied to doors with a note than presented face-to-face.

Tricky as response can be, Receivers wishing to undermine Bearers’ certainty or challenge their self-satisfaction can use #48 or #49, or a flippant #161. Those preferring to repudiate the Bearer than accept their sentiments have #103 or #37 with which to do so, or #30 with which to escalate hostilities if desired.

Tolerant or abashed Receivers, however, can accept the implicit reprimand with #137, #127, #151 or #122; #186 suggests both parties continue as normal, while #86 turns a criticism into a tease.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I have something to tell you
body:
The Bearer is brimming over with excitement, but cannot fully explain their reasons to the Receiver in their current situation – perhaps a gossipy workplace, or a public forum. Or perhaps the Bearer has a question that they must have the Receiver answer, post-haste. Often given in person with a meeting arranged between both parties in the near future, for the Receiver to then refuse, or be late to the meeting, is an act of considerable disrespect.

Often positive responses in kind are unnecessary, although #81 can be used; concerned Receivers can use #69 to ascertain the possible outcome of such discussions, #35 to insist on an unedited and fully disclosive answer, or #179 to playfully engage with the question at hand. #167 enquires about the Bearer’s emotional state; #128 indicates fear or #42 excited anticipation; #86 offers as assurance of the Receiver’s willingness to hear the news, and #33 promises respite if trouble is at hand.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You're imagining things
body:
Romance is a tricky beast, prone to leading mind and passions astray. Where one person may think a relationship entirely platonic, another may have desire in mind – and egos may be fractured as a result. Likewise, business and even friendship can be fraught with misunderstandings.

#22 can elegantly conceal exasperation or concern for a Receiver who has misread a situation and requires correction before further harm ensues. To send #27 in response is to apologise for whatever misunderstandings have occurred; #111 gives an incredulous dismissal; #87 promises whatever reparations are necessary. #122 dismisses the Bearer’s statement, while #137 agrees with it. #69 expresses concern over possibly destructive outcomes. #161 is an implicit shrug of the shoulders, while #163 asserts a potentially spurious innocence, and #154 makes platonic but friendly intentions clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: C'est la vie
body: Sometimes life just doesn’t work out as one has planned or wished, and #23 accepts and embraces this. Rather than being burdened with guilt, regret or worry, the Bearer wishes to express their acceptance of the current situation – be it forbidden love, financial woes, or a general and vague sense of ennui. Offering reassurance to the Receiver, it indicates that the Bearer will press on regardless, perhaps even with a spring in their step. As such, it often provides a mutually satisfactory conclusion to any conversation within which it appears. Should a Receiver wish to reply, #176 concedes defeat in the face of overwhelming odds; #146 asserts overwhelming discouragement; #137 acquiesces to the reasonableness of the Bearer’s position; #60 promises future satisfaction; and #83 offers gentle encouragement.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Help!
body:
Although this flower rarely refers to true peril, it is wise never to rule out such an eventuality. The Bearer has found themselves trapped in a situation or position from which they cannot extricate themselves alone, and stands in need of the Receiver’s assistance. Potentially they may even be trapped in a florist’s (as with #207), although in such cases some more precise geographical indication may be necessary. Concealment and a degree of subterfuge are often required to obfuscate the meaning from vigilant eyes. To ignore such a plea without inquiring further into the nature of the situation is unthinkable, and for that reason it should never be given spuriously.

Receivers wishing to assure the Bearer of their ongoing support can send #55 or #83 to do so, while #167 expresses concern and #97 or #89 ask simply what is needed. #94 offers conditional agreement, #132 wishes luck, #192 raises a cynical eyebrow, and #162 satisfaction for a job (hopefully) well done.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Don't call me, I'll call you
body: #25 cuts unpleasantly close to the bone. Dismissive and on occasion irritatingly superior, this Bearer wishes for no further contact with the Receiver unless for specific and exclusively self-determined purposes. Responding to such a communication is tricky – doing so is to violate the wishes of the Bearer, after all. #144 makes the Receiver’s anger at this treatment quite clear. #69 queries the Bearer’s decision, advisably or otherwise, whereas #98 and #80 disclaim the drama of the Bearer’s gesture, and #26 criticises their decision. #93, #91 or #30 can be used to shift the tone of such an exchange into a more directly confrontational mode, or #36 to express a final condemnation, but such Receivers should perhaps consider the possible results of their actions, and temper directness with caution.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Unwise
body: Whatever the Receiver’s intentions or actions have been, they have singularly failed to impress the Bearer. Whether encouragement to think twice about a professional venture, a personal dilemma or a romantic engagement, #26 provides maybe less-than-gentle encouragement to rethink the Receiver’s current course of action. Frequently, and perhaps unsurprisingly, Receivers are unreceptive to the Bearer’s advice, although those welcoming the Bearer’s criticism can acquiesce with #137 and give thanks with #121 or #134. Bearers can be courteously dismissed, however, with #140, or playfully with #163. Should the Receiver wish to assert superior knowledge of certain salient facts, #48 or a straightforward #37 make their position clear. A dismissive #184 or defiant #159 are appropriate for Receivers who stand by their behaviour, while #186 wryly acknowledges that the Bearer has a point, #195 offers compensation, #167 expresses concern and #168 redoubles a request.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Sorry
body:
This Bearer apologises unequivocally for any wrongdoing, accepts responsibility for any possible consequences, and perhaps seeks to make amends. To send #27 is to express complete surrender of the Bearer's side in any argument or dispute between the parties. Accordingly, it may be a powerful gesture, but #27 represents a great commitment, and should not be offered lightly. It can even be sent in advance of some iniquity on the part of the Bearer, although doing so requires careful timing and Receivers would be quite justified in sending #128 in response.

Benevolent Receivers can reply with #148 to offer a Bearer forgiveness, #186 to promise to ignore the relevant incident forthwith, or #57 or #86 to reassure the Bearer of their perceived ability to weather the storm. #11 pleads for caution; #124 implies the proffered abasement was long overdue; while #111 indicates disbelief. For those less than magnanimously inclined, #48, #138 and #144 explicitly refuse the proffered apology, #62 demands redress and #54 flatly asserts the Bearer’s ultimate untrustworthiness. Uncompromising dismissal can be sent with #122 or #25, whilst #91 explicitly reminds the Bearer of the sad inevitability of human consequences.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: For old times' sake?
body:
This affectionate and nostalgic message recalls old passion and times past, and perhaps speaks of a desire to return to them. Not necessarily romantic (although often used as such), the Bearer requests the Receiver to relive and rekindle the relationship they once shared; for a single drink, a single dinner, or a single amorous rendez-vous in secret. The precise nature of any such meeting is, of course, implied by the nature of the relationship that the parties once shared.

It is traditional for the Receiver to respond positively in kind, perhaps with #42, #124 or #151. If unsure of the Bearer’s meaning or intent – and perhaps a little wary, but keen to meet regardless - Receivers can respond with #11. Should acceptance be conditional, #94 provides means of saying so. #115 implicitly amplifies the sentiments occasioning the invitation in the first place. If affection is constant but circumstances prevent reunion, #67 or #95 may be appropriate. #177 or #184 give an unequivocal and somewhat crushing refusal, and #173 a somewhat more moderate version. Declining with #111 or #193 is rare, but on occasion peculiarly satisfying.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: This means war!
body:
Dangerous to bear, and perhaps even more dangerous to receive, this marks the opening of hostilities between the parties concerned; a resignation to use any and every means at the Bearer’s disposal to vanquish the Receiver.

Defiant Receivers can assert themselves with a challenging #107 or #86, a contemptuous #122 or #98, a disbelieving #111 or dismissive #165. Counter-threats are implicit in #93 and #144, whilst the roundly insulting #36 makes the Receiver’s opinion of the Bearer entirely clear. #185 suggests mistake, sarcastically or otherwise. #33 desires an end to the conflict, #43 concedes defeat; #49 counsels hesitation, and #132 courteously wishes an opponent luck; while #61 welcomes hostilities, and #42 invites the Bearer to do their worst.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Are you single?
body:
A simple question, indeed, but one with significant implications. The Bearer implies that they're interested in a relationship – whether long-term or otherwise – and should the Receiver reply in the affirmative, they will make their feelings known more directly.

Such an overture marks an excellent opportunity to let someone down gently, as a Receiver is free to say that they are, for example, in a relationship and unable to proceed as the Bearer would like – whether truthfully or otherwise.

To respond positively, a #73 has the virtue of simplicity, while #1 reassures the Bearer their sentiments are enthusiastically reciprocated and degrees of enthusiasm can be expressed through #65 or #5. #60 assures the Bearer that the Receiver will be at their service as soon as may be, and those whose situations call for a more sophisticated response than simply ‘yes’ or ‘no’ have #77 at their disposal. In stating unavailability, a regretful Bearer may respond with #17 or #95, whereas #37 requests the Bearer keep their curiosity to themselves in no uncertain terms, and #104 or even a simple #74 make the unlikelihood of any further engagement clear. Should the arrival of such a message have had negative consequences for the Receiver, they can make this clear to the Bearer with a direct #138.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: CSV notes field: Still not that happy with the title of this one. Earlier titles: "Single?" (5.1)

title: Truce
body:
In times of hardship, tension, grief or trouble, Bearer and Receiver have found themselves at loggerheads, beset by arguments, worry, and the harsh constraints of reality. For this Bearer, affection for the Receiver outweighs the difficulties of a situation, prompting the suggestion of calling a halt to hostilities for a while. Whether the respite in question consists of a trip away or merely an agreed period where all discussion of difficulties must cease, #33 offers shared escape, however temporarily.

Receivers wishing to convey understanding of the situation and acquiesce with the Bearer’s request can do so with #137; #94 offers conditional acceptance; while #54 refuses on grounds of the Bearer’s untrustworthiness. #44 makes it clear that matters are at breaking point, while a more optimistic #61 suggests this could be a significant new beginning.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Respite" (Code Generator)

title: I love you
body: Passion, devotion, kinship, desire, idolatry, yearning, rapture; love is infinitely various as those who live it, and #34 is an intensely joyous celebration of its truth. The Bearer wishes the Receiver to know of their adoration, body and soul. Often only responding in kind is necessary, but the profound feeling in #115 and #152, the devotion of #4 and #197, the newfound enchantment of #59, commitment of #66 or simple contentment of #106 are all significant in themselves. #157 expresses childlike joy, while #46 or #47 affirm the bond between Bearer and Receiver. #163 responds with a teasing self-deprecation, while #124 implies that the expression of such sentiments are long overdue, and #62 demands the Bearer prove their love. #54 states baldly the Receiver’s mistrust of the Bearer, whilst an advisory #11, #65 or #49 counsel caution. Receivers substantially less than overjoyed at the receipt of such assertions, however, can send in repudiation an unequivocal #48 or #184. #104 provides a semi-apologetic explanation, while the blank incomprehension of #98 or #78 prove effective if destructive means of undercutting the Bearer’s declaration.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: April 2013 book layout text differs (similarity 0.921; mainly layout trims/reference formatting).

title: Tell me the truth
body:
Something, somewhere, is wrong; a note is off key; this Bearer is suspicious. #35 is a bold request, not just implying deception or prevarication from the Receiver, but demanding the entire, unedited truth, about both the Receiver's actions and their view of the Bearer. Frequently, this offers the welcome opportunity to bring troublesome matters into the open, clear up any misunderstandings and bring subsumed tensions bubbling to the surface. However, sending #35 can also require both certainty and wisdom, for it is undoubtedly true that sometimes current upset and confusion may in fact be preferable to an unpalatable unalloyed truth.

Receivers wishing to continue the invited dialogue may reply with #114. #55 assures the Bearer they have no need for concern, and #60 promises future fulfilment, if only the Bearer can wait a while.

Perhaps the ideal response, should such a gesture come from a romantic partner, is #57, although #46 may also ring true.

Those wishing to refuse the Bearer’s request, however, may use #37 or #67; although, as always, such a powerful gesture of repudiation should only be made after thought and deliberation.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Go and die in a hole
body:
The Bearer is somewhat disenchanted with the Receiver. Relations may have been damaged by unexpected revelation (#72 or #104, perhaps?), ongoing tension or sudden distress, and #36 endeavours to communicate a consequent explicit rejection. Those wishing to echo the Bearer’s sentiments have #171 with which to do so, while those considering the Bearer’s message as an opening of hostilities may use #30 or #52 to convey this. Dismissal of the intended sentiment’s importance can be conveyed through #86, or its fervour can be ironically accepted with #100.

Puzzlement or a request for explanation are articulated through #194 or #163, while Receivers wishing to open negotiations, wisely or otherwise, can send #51 or even a wistful #118 to do so. #126 or #162, on the other hand, offer perfect means of disregarding the Bearer’s feelings.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Go die in a hole" (Code Generator)

title: Mind your own business
body:
Sometimes subtlety is the wrong approach. Somewhat rude, perhaps, but occasionally necessary when dealing with an improper or needlessly persistent enquirer.

Possible responses are varied. Receivers accepting themselves to be at fault may use #27 or #137, while those understandably regarding such a gift as a hostile gesture have #30 or a laconic #178 at their disposal. Confusion as to the rationale for such a dramatic dismissal can be communicated with #194, and those eager to pursue their enquiries despite the Bearer’s reluctance can send #167 or even #168 in an effort at persuasion.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Unworthy
body:
Flattery indeed! Such a gift speaks volumes of the humility of the Bearer, whose high regard for the Receiver is such that they are convinced a preferable partner or collaborator for them could easily be found. Not necessarily romantic, but often used as such, the desired response is frequently one of blushing refutation, and often delivery of the same message in return: an assertion in some sense that the Receiver feels similarly undeserving of the Bearer. Literal-minded or unenamoured Receivers, however, may take this as both a compliment and an excuse to look elsewhere. Be careful!

Compliments to send in response abound. Affectionate remonstrance is evident in #95; romantic acceptance in #13 or #46; cheeky concurrence in #62; or fond compliment in #196.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Lips sealed
body: Silence can be of the utmost importance; here a Bearer swears to keep whatever indiscretion or potentially dangerous secret that the Receiver has entrusted them with quiet for as long as necessary. It makes an excellent response to flowers such as #67, #93 and #17 – all of which place the Bearer in the graces of the Receiver. Of course, should the Bearer subsequently break their promise – no matter what the situation, or the duress that they are placed under – then they will have to work hard to regain their standing, and for their word to carry any weight in future. #39 can also be used to instruct the Receiver to keep silent - a sensible move, providing the Receiver is minded to do so. Bearers should beware of receiving #67, #111, #98 or even #113 in reply.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I can wait
body:
A noble intent; the Bearer assures the Receiver they will wait for as long as necessary for a decision to be made or a course of action to become viable. Whether sent by potential lovers, separated sweethearts or simply between friends awaiting confidence and conversation, #41 indicates resolution on the Bearer’s part, and considerable esteem for the Receiver. Should the process take more than a year, the Bearer is encouraged to send #41 every year on the same date, if acceptable, to show that they still hold the Receiver in their regard. To send #41 is to say that the Bearer will wait forever and a day, and is often a forlorn assertion of a love or desire that cannot be attained.

Receivers can indicate simple gratitude with #121, proffer reassurance of their devotion with #4, #46 or #60, impose conditions with #94, or disengage themselves from the Bearer with #67. #83 requests the Bearer not abandon hope just yet, while #42 suggests the proposed delay is intolerable. #103, #25 and #111 all offer brutal means of repudiating the Bearer’s regard, but it is advisable for Receivers to be entirely certain before doing so, as Bearers are unlikely to forgive such slights.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I can't wait
body:
Half familiar, breathless, restless longing, half exasperated reluctance to spend another day in turmoil; if this message arrives prior to an arranged meeting, a clear addendum is attached - I can't wait to meet you - and thus conveys excitement, joy and exuberant anticipation of the encounter.

Should this be the case, #157, #171 or #19 may all be suitable replies. However, if given in response to a more delicate message – perhaps #83, #57 or #51 – it slants dramatically towards I won't wait, and takes on a far harsher tone. If so, #51 appeals the decision. #91 warns of potential trouble as a result, #44 asserts the limits of the Receiver’s tolerance in militant terms, and #60 promises great reward should the Bearer choose patience, whereas #69 expresses concern over the possible consequences of their haste.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You win
body:
An acceptance of failure, perhaps, or an acknowledgement of victory – #43 can mean both, in the right circumstances. Whilst it may be used to playfully declare submission to a beloved’s temptations, or to honour the conclusion of a prolonged tussle between friends, a more commonplace meaning is an admission of defeat and a call for hostilities to cease. A humble sentiment indeed, and should it be accepted by the Receiver, one that should be honoured by both parties.

#154 offers dignified means of accepting such a surrender, while #84 gives a somewhat pitying edge. #131, #162 or #20 celebrate the Bearer’s triumph; #71 queries the strength of their resolution; #98 disclaims the victory entirely, while #109 acknowledges the one’s opponent’s worth and #173 courteously wishes them future success. #186 proposes mutual denial of whatever occasioned the Bearer’s gesture. If the Receiver in fact wishes the Bearer to persist – in opposition, seduction or whatever conflict prompted their surrender – #83 may be sent to tell them so.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: One last chance
body:
Either this Bearer has been hurt before (by the Receiver, or by others they consider of a similar bent) and is issuing a warning, or they are a supplicant, all too aware of the Receiver's history and nevertheless desiring a single opportunity to prove themselves.

Bearers issuing an ultimatum are possessed of generally positive sentiments regarding the Receiver, but all too aware of potential difficulties, wishing both to caution the Receiver and perhaps to gently establish the upper hand from the start. It is considered courteous of the Bearer to ensure the Receiver knows the precise nature of any situation prompting such a gift, as well as what constitutes a mistake. Failure to do so, except in the all-too-frequent and frustrating circumstances where such knowledge eludes the Receiver, is the height of bad manners. Likewise, it is exceedingly inappropriate for those pleading for licence to do so unless they are reasonably certain of their ability to fulfil such a promise.

Should the Receiver wish to convey acceptance and understanding, #53 or #137 allow them to do so; #55 promises additional support and protection. If the Receiver feels responsible for the Bearer’s pain, #113 accepts this and offers a profound apology, #183 promises never to repeat their actions, #195 promises reparation, and #140 begs for renewed trust. On the other hand #98 or #184 sharply repudiate the whole idea - albeit in sufficiently stark terms that a Bearer may well wish to retract any accord, conditional or otherwise. #11 or #77 suggest both parties should conduct themselves with care, whereas #94 answers the Bearer’s terms with conditions of the Receiver’s own, and #178 wryly or humorously acknowledges the implicit finality of the Bearer’s assertion.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Body cites #82, which is not an entry in any source (unresolved also in the April 2013 book layout). April 2013 book layout text differs (similarity 0.867; mainly layout trims/reference formatting).

title: That was wonderful
body:
Whether given in thanks for a night in company, a romantic gesture, a friendly helping hand or an act of unexpected generosity, #45 is a precious and powerful gesture of appreciation, by a Bearer pleased and moved by the Receiver. Implicit is the desire to repeat the experience, whatever it may have been, as soon as may be.

Romantically-minded Receivers wishing to declare their feelings can reply with #34, #13, #120, #59 or #106, while those newer to one another have a cordial #151, an appreciative #121 or a noncommittal #96 at their disposal, and #11 or #77 warn of possible pitfalls ahead.

Receivers fundamentally disagreeing with the Bearer’s assessment have a teasing #109, or #162, an unequivocal #25, #111 or #104, or a troubled #149 to communicate their disappointment.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I'm yours
body:
A powerful and passionate declaration often all too casually scattered. This Bearer offers themselves fully to the Receiver in terms of time, attention and love; in effect, giving the Receiver priority over all others, even themselves, in all things.

Such a sentiment is not to be declared lightly, nor treated frivolously by the Receiver. Appropriate responses include #47, a straightforward reflection of the sentiment, or #66 or #34, almost equally passionate, if less decisive, assertions of devotion. #55 or #57 offer reassurance regardless of any troubles the parties may be suffering, while #62 teasingly demands the Bearer prove the truth of their message. #38 speaks of a Receiver perceiving themselves unworthy of the Bearer’s devotion, and #160 of one doubting its validity; #124, however, implies the Receiver had been waiting quite some time for such an assertion, and #131 implies the intent to use it to mischievous effect.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You're mine
body: An assertion of possession remarkable for its intensity; no choice, no negotiation, no escape. #47 can often demonstrate reciprocal feeling and shared trust - but always with a darker edge, redolent of loss of control or a possibly troubling lack of autonomy. Receivers willing to surrender may do so with #46, #168 or the absolute dedication of #87, while #94 offers the opportunity to impose conditions on such self-abnegation. Those resistant to the Bearer’s charms, however, can express reluctance with #71, disbelief with #111 or a self-deprecating #163, or somewhat ironic defiance with an offhand #132, #180 or #188.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Big mistake
body: A grave error has been made somewhere along the line, and the Bearer wishes to disabuse the Receiver of mistaken notions. Nor do they feel the need to pull their punches in communicating the fact - either urgency or animosity compels their hand. Receivers denying their culpability can send #174, those accepting it #185, or any bemused by such an assertion #194 or #80. Concern can be expressed with #69 or #91; those doubting the Bearer can do so with #111. Often a response, #48 usually signals either conflict or resolution. #159 or #161 suggest whatever mistakes have been made were worthwhile; #77 points out the complexity of whatever situation Bearer and Receiver find themselves in; while #49 requests the Bearer pause for thought or reconsideration.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Cardinal error" (5.1)

title: Hold your horses
body:
Human relationships are fraught with differences in opinion and perspective, and love in particular is a notoriously difficult business. When passions run high, it can be all too easy for enthusiasm, confusion or lust to overtake reasoned thought or objectiveness. The Bearer of #49 realises such a misunderstanding has occurred; either informing the other party, or acknowledging their own mistake. Such Bearers are keen to make amends, and seek to remain on good terms with the Receiver, but remain unashamed of their original motivations.

Receivers sympathetic to the Bearers of such messages may offer #53 in assurance of their continued regard; the romantically minded have #57 or #34 at their disposal; whilst more troubled or despondent Receivers can send #114, #118 or #116 to indicate a desire to renegotiate or further discuss. #42 signals either refutation or impatience, #137 accepts the Bearer’s concern; while #41 speaks of a Receiver willing to exercise patience and #163 assumes an innocence which may or may not be applicable. #168 pleads for reconsideration, #111 declares disbelief, but a simple #137 accepts the Bearer’s good sense entirely.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Anything but that
body: Thus speaks a Bearer ready to submit to anything save what the Receiver proposes. Not to be sent without due consideration, for the Receiver may demand whatever they choose in return, #51 can be as playful or as serious as the parties concerned choose to make it. #160 is particularly relevant in response, but #131, #93, and #47 may also express important responses. #71 questions the Bearer’s certainty, #107 disregards their caution, while #195 offers reparation and #184 remains stoutly unsympathetic to the Bearer’s declaration.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You lose
body:
An unashamed declaration of victory over the Receiver, whether in love or war. Should such an unabashedly triumphant message be sent, it is courteous for hostilities to cease immediately.

Receivers can accept the Bearer’s victory with #43 or #86, or reject it with #111 or a spurious #163. #30 declares the commencement of further hostilities, #118 laments the conflict, whilst profound negative effects are acknowledged with #146, #128 or #144. #176 concedes defeat, while #181 stoutly refuses to do so. #93 issues a threat, and #131 implies one, as well as neatly undercutting the Bearer’s certainty. #165 disclaims a Bearer’s putative immaturity for asserting such a victory, while #23 or #161 express resignation. #44 asks for a last chance, #33 for a break, and #159 declares that whatever contest the parties have been engaged in was more than worthwhile.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I understand
body:
Whatever is troubling the Receiver, the Bearer of #53 wishes to offer them unconditional acceptance and support, whatever the cost to themselves. Whilst often sent in unhappy circumstances – refusal, rejection, a parting of ways – this is perhaps never entirely negative, as it signals sufficient care and consideration on the part of the Bearer to appreciate and accept the Receiver’s concerns.

Receivers unconvinced of the Bearer’s understanding can use #193 to express their doubts. #134 and #121 express gratitude, whereas depending on the relationship between Bearer and Receiver #57 or #139 may be appropriate. #23 indicates wry acceptance, #11 begs the Bearer to take care, while those wishing to repel the Bearer’s concern have #103, #37 or #111 with which to make themselves quite clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I don't trust you
body: An emphatic rejection of faith in the Bearer’s integrity, this is often a pivotal point in any relationship. Whilst capable of being either playful or serious in meaning - as part of a teasing exchange with #120 and #62, or following #131, for example - it can also be crucial in response to #118, say, or #57, and is often hard to respond to. Those wishing to assert the importance of the Bearer to them have #152 to do so, or those feeling the need to apologise have #113, or maybe #27. If such a statement requires explanation, #80 or #12 offer means of asking for it, whereas Receivers simply anxious the Bearer know the effect of their mistrust have #146, and #149 with which to do so. #194 enquires as to the Receiver’s culpability for such mistrust. Perhaps #69 is the most poignant question arising from #54. Should the initial gesture have been more teasing than tortured, however, #163 or #107 may be suitable in response.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: And my axe!
body:
Whether a Receiver’s troubles are romantic, professional, personal or simply the result of long-term stresses and strains, this Bearer simply wants them to know they’re not alone; whatever happens, there’s another person on their side. And a recommissioned, possibly sharpened, gardening tool. A gesture of friendship rather than passion, #55 invites trust and companionship from the Receiver.

Responding may be as simple as #121 or #134, or the wry acknowledgement of #101. #18 communicates trust in the Bearer, while lovers may reply with #34, #4, #152 or #57.

Cynical Receivers may employ #160, #54 or even #48 to question the reality of the Bearer’s assertion.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "I'm here/And my axe" (5.1)

title: Adventure
body:
The Bearer wishes to take the Receiver away, somewhere, for excitement and escapism; the precise destination, and the adventure’s precise duration and nature is left up to the Bearer to explain upon the Receiver's acceptance.

In fact, keeping the details deliberately secret is encouraged to heighten anticipation, and if the Receiver agrees without knowing what the future holds for them, it is a sign of a strong connection and trust between both parties.

Receivers wishing to impose conditions upon their acceptance have #94 with which to do so, while #98 or #111 articulate disbelief and #124 the decided belief that the Bearer’s offer comes none too soon. #157 or #42 express enthusiasm, while those communicate a hedonistic wish for new experiences can send #105 in order to do so. #188 refuses politely, #180 and #181 somewhat less so; #17 expresses regret, and #67 the firm conviction of inappropriateness.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: CSV notes field: I never really liked this title...

title: We can get through this
body:
Life is not always as easy as one would like, and sending #57 acknowledges that – but whether the difficulties are financial, romantic or familial, this Bearer knows that the bond of love between the two parties will keep them strong throughout.

Although admitting that something is amiss, and that one needs help to make it right, is frequently difficult, it can also be crucial to successfully negotiating trouble, especially if problems lie within the relationship between Bearer and Receiver. It is a forgiving message, suggesting growth and optimistic evolution, and Receivers should be pleased that they are bound to such an understanding partner.

Reassurance of the Receiver’s willingness to bear with the situation can be given with #83 or #86, while #87 promises to do whatever it takes to improve matters.

Receivers despairing of the Bearer’s promise can use #146 to articulate their sorrow, while sadness for the state of things is evident in #149 or a lamenting #118.

#152 asserts the Receiver’s need for the Bearer, and those wishing to underline their love and care can send #34 or #140 to do so. Doubtful Receivers can remain equivocal with #71, whilst #160 and #193 express disagreement and #177 or #176 disclaim any desire to try.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "I know this is difficult, but I love you and we can survive" (5.1)

title: I've never felt this way before
body:
This Bearer is overwhelmed by their feelings, whether by an unexpected sense of understanding or attraction with a new partner, unprecedented concord or security with an old one, or simply the introduction of hitherto unexplored depths into a previously harmonious but limited connection. New feelings are awakening, and the Bearer revels in it.

For some Receivers, a loving #46 or #47 may seem appropriate in response, while for others #34, #86 or #87 may be more apt. A playful #62 invites further demonstration of the Bearer’s feelings, while #124 teasingly accepts their gesture, #12 invites explanation and #11 counsels caution.

Should either Bearer or Receiver’s feelings be negative, a kindly #154, a troubling #49 or a despondent #149 all communicate the fact.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: 2014 press release says this is "three roses and three gerberas" (222555), but 222555 is #118 in the CSV; CSV code 2255 = two roses, two gerberas. Earlier titles: "I've never felt like this before*" (Code Generator)

title: Patience
body:
An assurance that only inconvenient circumstance prevents the Bearer from devoting themselves utterly to the Receiver. Should the latter be prepared to wait, once extricated either by their own hand or the passage of time said Bearer will give themselves utterly. Whilst such a gesture is evidently romantic, only Receiver and Bearer can judge how much patience may be necessary - and how long they are prepared to wait.

Receivers adamant that the Bearer is worth waiting for and wishing to provide assurance of their love have #34, #66, #4 or #87 to declare themselves, whereas those overwhelmed by their feelings for the Bearer can communicate this with #19. #86 speaks of a Receiver eminently willing to endure delay for the Bearer’s sake, while #95 or #160 indicate disbelief. Those for whom the Bearer’s circumstances are particularly troubling or tragic can send #145 or #146, while #57 or #83 assure the Bearer that the desire to wait is mutual. #176, #54 or #62 all speak of a Receiver at the end of their tether, and any Bearers receiving these in return should be wary lest they lose the object of their professed patience.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Patience (once I'm free, I'm yours)" (5.1)

title: And so it begins...
body: Whether threat or promise, this Bearer wishes to mark the start of something: the opening of hostilities, or a blossoming romance; seduction, or destruction. A Receiver’s response evidently depends on unfolding events: a newfound intimacy might require #59 or #45, and an amorous campaign could be encouraged with #19 or refused with #22. Incipient threat can be acknowledged with #26, brought to a premature ceasefire with #33. #93 predicts peril ahead, #128 communicates the Receiver’s fear, #98 their confusion or #42 their keen anticipation.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Code Generator.xlsx (Jan 2013) gives code 2233, CSV gives 11122. Earlier titles: "It begins" (5.1)

title: Prove it
body:
Challenge indeed; from a Bearer sufficiently confident in a Receiver’s devotion to tease, but wishing nevertheless for practical demonstrations of their passion. Whether the demand is met through prearranged methods or the impulse of the moment, the outcome of such a gesture can often be revealing for both Bearer and Receiver, and should therefore be issued with care.

Should the Receiver feel the Bearer seeks traditionally romantic affirmation, sending #34, #19, #4 or #46 may come in useful, whereas those planning a lengthy campaign in response can use #61 or #30 to warn its object. Reluctant Receivers can refuse with #74, or #111, or make their negative responses clear with #165, while enthusiastic ones can both embrace the challenge and ask for suggestions with #97 or #87.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Show me how much you love me" (5.1)

title: We want different things
body: Sometimes needs, desires or lives pull in different directions; it’s nobody’s fault, but togetherness becomes impossible. Sorrowful Receivers can concur with the truth of this statement with #118, or accuse the Bearer with #116, request clarity with #80, #69 or #35 or suggest reasons with #72; express grief with #146, or beg a last chance with #44. #63 can, of course, also provide sound reason for not attempting involvement in the first place, in which case #137 and #161 provide dignified means of response.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Rest easy
body: This Bearer wishes peace and succour to a Receiver beset by circumstances, sleeping fitfully if at all due to worry, insomnia or simply stress. More concerned with recommending relaxation and rejuvenation than providing the ongoing encouragement of #117, appropriate responses range from the gratitude of #121 to the acknowledgement and loving reassurance of #57, with the somewhat more confrontational options of #122 or #37 should the Bearer’s attentions be unwanted. #86 assures the Bearer that however difficult their situation, they have it under control.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Sleep well, rest easy" (5.1, 5.4, 5.5, Code Generator)

title: Slow down
body:
While this Bearer appreciates the attention that they're getting, it is perhaps a little too much to take in; hopefully, if the Receiver understands the message, they will steady their hand and approach the situation with more caution and forethought than before.

Receivers should not despair; while this sometimes implies fear that the nature of a relationship is progressing at too rapid a rate, it can just as easily mean that the Bearer is receiving far too many messages from the Receiver and cannot find time to respond properly to them all! Whilst given the nature of the message some delay in responding may be appropriate, sending #53 makes their acceptance of the Bearer’s position clear.

Receivers startled or disturbed at such an instruction can communicate this with #116 or #118, but those recognising some truth to the Bearer’s hesitation can use #27 to apologise.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Forever yours
body:
A noble sentiment, perhaps as close to lifelong devotion as this turbulent world will allow. The Bearer of this message is certain they wish to remain by the Receiver’s side for as long as they both shall live; passion, adoration and love.

Echoing the Bearer’s gift, or a simple #73, is often all that’s required, but #34 or #46 might be appropriate. In the unfortunate circumstance that the Bearer’s sentiments are not echoed, #76 or #27 can be used to give a gentle letdown, while #22, #154 and #111 are somewhat more unequivocal and #188 uncompromisingly dismissive.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Till death do us part" (5.1)

title: It would be wrong
body:
For reasons beyond their control, this Bearer cannot hope to go along with the Receiver’s wishes. Since such obstacles are frequently matters of religion, creed or some similarly sensitive subject, and thus insurmountable, it is recommended that the Receiver not push for an answer as to why the arrangement cannot go ahead in greater detail.

However, should such clarity be desired, then #80 may be sent, although Bearers are advised to bear in mind the possible consequences of such unmediated honesty before doing so. More sensible, perhaps, would be to respond with a graceful #137, #81 or #53. If challenge is required, #107 provides it; #140 assures their concerns are groundless, while #49 gently suggests a misunderstanding has occurred and #48 robustly declares the Bearer has made an error.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Is this the end?
body:
Bearer and Receiver are estranged for some reason; each lost and uncertain of what the future might hold. Sending #69 can be an attempt at restitution or a request to confirm an already-realised loss; replies evidently vary greatly depending on the Receiver’s feelings for the Bearer.

Those wishing to disagree emphatically can send #57 or #51, or even #46. #63 and #116 not only agree but give reasons, while further information can be requested with #153 or #194. #21 and #114 both propose a potentially negative conversation, #44 makes the desperation of the situation wholly apparent, and #76 expresses simple uncertainty. #33 suggests momentary respite for both parties to gather their thoughts; #176 and #177 concede defeat; #182 declares parting inevitable, while #184 unsympathetically instructs the Bearer to adjust swiftly to such a conclusion.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Sure thing
body: This Bearer's lighthearted certainty is infectious. An affirmative connoting joy and enthusiasm, #70 is usually welcome - unless, perhaps, where preceded by #30 or #176. Cutting in response to #69, #188 or #114, it can also be used to echo the sentiments of #161 or #154, respond unequivocally to #3 or #56, or touchingly enthuse in reply to #208. Receivers may find #131, #116, #162, #148 or a laconic #147 useful in the tricky matter of composing a reply.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Reluctance
body: For whatever reason, this Bearer is unwilling to accede to the Receiver’s wishes; similar ventures may have miscarried previously, they feel possible consequences have been ill considered, or perhaps an unambiguous #131 or #107 has set them on their guard. Perhaps they need the reassurance of #105, #140 or #34, or the invitation to discussion in #80; perhaps further exposition of the Receiver’s feelings, such as #152 or #4, will help set their mind at rest. #41 offers an assurance that the Receiver will wait as long as it takes, and #87 that they’re prepared to do anything to convince the Bearer. #12 indicates confusion at the Bearer’s uncertainty, #168 a plea, and #22 suggests the Bearer’s reluctance results from nothing more dramatic than an overactive imagination.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: CSV notes field: This may instead be called Earlier titles: "If you're sure..." (Code Generator)

title: Someone else?
body: Never an easy matter to discuss, whether informing or asking, and often one to which no answer is entirely comforting (for something, if not a rival, must have occasioned the troubling behaviour prompting the question...) but so often a pivotal moment. Whether the Bearer regards the prospect of an affirmative answer as liberating or catastrophic, whether the Receiver chooses to respond with a simple #73 or #74, the passionate reassurance of #46, a regretful #27, an imploring #113, a threatening #93 or a defiant #144 or #48, the consequences of such an enquiry - or assertion - are rarely trivial. #174 suggests there is an alternative explanation, #186 proposes total denial by both parties, #37 informs the Bearer in no uncertain terms that such matters are none of their concern, while #195 promises potentially dubious compensation and #95 contains the less-than-reassuring implication that the chance would be a fine thing.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Yes
body: An affirmative with certainty and weight; whatever question the Receiver has asked, or request made, this Bearer will agree without even the conditionals of #80. Happy Receivers can show their feelings with #157 or #134, show gratitude with #121, or advise caution with #160. Receivers with plans about which they feel the Bearer may not be entirely enthusiastic can signal this with #131 or #61, or should a question have been negative (#69 or #72, for example), a Receiver can share their feelings with #149, #146, #36 or #145.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: No
body: A simple but quite unequivocal refusal of whatever the Bearer is proposing. No further explanation or negotiation is necessarily required, although in certain circumstances (say, when #74 has arrived in response to #154 or #153) it is certainly churlish. Receivers can make such requests with #80, #35 or perhaps #168, or appeal the Bearer’s decision with #168; if they accept the Bearer’s choice, #137, #122 or #53 all make this courteously explicit. Should they wish either to inform the Bearer of a perceived error, #48 or #26 do so, whilst the explicitly hostile #30 or #131 can be as serious or teasing as Bearer and Receiver require.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Unsure
body:
Confusion lies at the heart of this message, and the way forward will not be clear for some time. The Bearer feels unable to commit to a single course of action and instead must weigh their options – but sending such a message requires care and scrupulous honesty. To proffer #76 merely as a delaying tactic in a situation one finds uncomfortable marks the Bearer as inconsiderate, uncaring of the feelings, and time, of others.

Receivers sympathetic to the Bearer’s plight can signal their acceptance with #53, whereas those left in difficult situations can articulate their emotional unease with #11.

Those intent on an answer from the Receiver have #44 to signal the limits of their tolerance, and those left confused can use #118 or #12 to request further insight.

Angry or frustrated Receivers, however, have #144, #93, #36, #101 or #48 to express themselves.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: It's complicated
body: Often, particularly in matters of the heart, delicate situations can be too complex for easy explanation, particularly to the casual enquirer. Whilst #77 does not necessarily constitute a refusal to engage with the Receiver, it does at least indicate that further contact and explanation is required should they wish to pursue the connection. Responding with a courteous #81 or #53 is polite, but does not invite further conversation as #80 might. Those asking for the sake of romantic interest can send #1 or #181 to make their positions clear, whereas a #154 in response declares a consequent lack of romantic intent. #89 offers assistance, #87 asserts the Bearer’s willingness to do whatever it takes to placate or assist the Receiver, and #41 speaks of a Receiver willing to wait for as long as it takes for matters to resolve themselves. #35 declares an admirable desire for the absolute truth, #71 suggests uncertainty, whilst a challenging #175 or #183, or an unequivocal #177 or #186 approach the situation in martial terms. Sometimes, however, only a laconic #192 will do.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Tell me more
body:
Further information is required. A Receiver’s behaviour has been troubling or out of character, or they have promised an explanation yet to be forthcoming; messages have been exchanged and the Bearer is puzzled as to their implications; discussions have been evasive or inconclusive.

Perhaps #114 is the simplest way of facilitating an appropriate resolution, but underlying emotional resonance can be addressed through the reassurance offered by #174 or #4, or while #37, #39, #54, #180 or #77 make it resolutely and sometimes gleefully clear the Bearer’s curiosity will remain unsatisfied. #186 suggests both parties deny the entire request and continue as normal.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Of course
body: To this Bearer, the answer, or the truth of a situation, is obvious. Of course they love (or hate) the Receiver; of course they’ll see them soon; of course there is danger ahead. Whilst often useful in response to requests for assistance such as #15 or #24, or to gratefully acquiesce to declarations or cessations of hostility, #81 can prompt answers from the grateful #121 or #134 to the grave #116 or ominous #11 or #114, and its undertones of certainty should perhaps be deployed with care.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Don't give up
body: A serious message of encouragement to a Receiver in need of succour and support due to the professional pressures, personal trauma, or the ongoing stresses and strains of life. #45 and #134 thank the Bearer for their concern, while #55 declares intent to continue in martial terms and #86 the ability to cope. #57 is appropriate for lovers whose relationship is placed under strain by the issues in question, whereas #101 and #24 more-or-less humorously beg the Bearer’s assistance and #176 or #177 playfully declare surrender. #191 implicitly promises support, and #198 recognises the Bearer’s undoubted charm, generosity and kindness.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Don't give up/Keep calm" (5.1)

title: Condolences
body: #84 often expresses the Bearer’s heartfelt sympathies for whatever griefs and troubles a Receiver is suffering. Dignified, without the need for romantic or intimate closeness, #84 is often the only possible response to tragic events, and a simple #121 serves to thank the donor. Should the Receiver be in desperate straits, #24, #146 or #152 can be used to communicate this. Of course, #84 can also be used as an ironic response to a Receiver prone to complaining, in which case an exchange more noted for its silliness than its sentiment may well ensue. #192, #122, or #78 may all come in useful here.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Condolence" (Code Generator)

title: I can take it
body:
No matter what the Receiver desires, whatever the cost, this Bearer will accept. Whether offering reassurance in anticipation of a clearly troubling revelation or declaring one’s willingness to perform whatever task the Receiver may require, #86 is an unequivocal statement of dedication to the Receiver.

Context is paramount. Whilst a relieved or thankful Receiver may prefer the simple gratitude of #121 or the genuine appreciation of #134, a Receiver with mischievous intent may find #131, #93 or a cynical #160 appropriate, or offer appropriate compensation for the imposition in question with #195.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I'll do anything
body: This Bearer surrenders self, will and desire to the Receiver - whatever they want, the Bearer will perform. It is not unusual for Receivers to send #160 in return, forcing the Bearer to confront the magnitude of their intentions, but #120, #62 or #100 give clear instructions to the Bearer; #131 communicates effectively that the Bearer may not know what they’re in for, while #95 and #111 emphatically question the Bearer’s wisdom, and #65 advises caution. #188 or #25, however, reject the Bearer’s offer in no uncertain terms, and #177 declares a cataclysmic end to proceedings.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Can I help?
body:
This Bearer wishes to do whatever is in their power to help a Receiver lost, troubled or beset by circumstance. A seemingly selfless gesture, asking nothing in return save the pleasure of having given assistance, responses can vary from a simple #121 to an enthusiastic #134. #124 suggests the Bearer’s offer is somewhat tardy, #15 requests assistance in return, and #77 implies matters may be more complex than the Bearer is currently aware. #24 or #152 emphatically and affectionately request the Bearer make good their offer, while #76 expresses uncertainty or vacillation.

Should the Bearer’s offer be unfortunately impossible for some reason, #95 or #149 make the Receiver’s regret clear, while #188 is openly dismissive.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Consequences
body:
Albeit rather caring than challenging, #91 is nevertheless a powerful warning of impending injury or damage done. This Bearer strongly advises the Receiver to reconsider a course of action they perceive as inadvisable at best.

Receivers confident in their actions and in their awareness of all aspects of a situation can reject the Bearer’s concern with a firm #86; reprimand them with #22 or #37; query the warning with a noncommittal #80 or #98; thank the Bearer with #121 or offer further, if difficult, information with #114. #117 proffers perhaps the best method of proceeding, whatever the circumstances.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: April 2013 book layout text differs (similarity 0.965; mainly layout trims/reference formatting).

title: Danger
body: Trouble lies ahead, for both Bearer and Receiver; this constitutes a warning to think very carefully about the possible consequences of one’s actions. Whether sent in the context of an ongoing hostile exchange or a serious conversation, it is always advisable to pay attention to the warning contained herein. Responses vary from the disbelieving #98 or #111 to the puzzled #12, the possibly foolhardy #86, the passionate #87 or the dismissive #122. #128 communicates fear and acceptance of the Bearer’s warning, while #193 denies its validity.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: On one condition
body: Whatever request Receiver has made of the Bearer, there is at least one stipulation to be made before they agree. Perhaps the Receiver has hurt the Bearer previously, or failed to take into consideration some crucial point; perhaps they are negotiating the future terms of a relationship, and the Bearer has a dealbreaker to share. Responses can vary from the unequivocally positive #81 to the decidedly negative #111 or #98, whilst the romantic #4, #152 or #18 make the Receiver’s feelings clear. Senders of #86 are confident in their capacity to meet the Bearer’s demands, those using #87 will do whatever it takes, #80 requests explanation and #23 accepts the situation, while #51 speaks of a Receiver prepared to do anything except that which the Bearer asks.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: If only
body: Whether with passionate longing or merely wistfulness, this Bearer wishes it were so. Often a response to the romantic desperation of #17 or the concern of #57, as well as modest refutation of compliments or invitations, suitable replies are many and varied. #140 urges the Bearer to trust the Receiver, while #149 and #146 convey regret and despair at how matters have turned out. #87 asserts that the Receiver will go to any extremes should the Bearer require, while #23 and #161 ruefully accept the inevitability of some of life’s misfortunes and impossibilities.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: See you soon
body: A straightforward assurance that the Bearer is keenly anticipating reunion with the Receiver. As appropriate between acquaintances as lovers, such a message is more friendly than fevered, expressing appreciation of the Receiver’s company without the longing overtones of #19, say, or #152. If appropriate, Receivers can respond in kind, or echo the Bearer’s enthusiasm with #42, #115 or #157; if otherwise, #116 implies a shift in the relationship has left the Receiver bereft, and #35 requests honesty about how or why; #139 perhaps increases the intimacy of such an exchange, reminding the Bearer they are in the Receiver’s thoughts; #123 or #1 add a note of romantic appreciation; #117 or #83 offers support to a Bearer under pressure; #55 reinforces a friendship; whereas #111, #67, #71 or #104 all make the Receiver’s intention to spurn the Bearer’s invitation clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: What do?
body:
Thus speaks a Bearer entirely at a loss for word or deed, and desirous of the Receiver’s instruction and assistance.

#117 offers a calm, sensible suggestion for how to proceed; while further detail can be requested with #80. #55 assures the Bearer of the Receiver’s support and #114 proposes a potentially tricky conversation. Those placed in a difficult situation by such a query can express this with #127 or #77, while Receivers unwilling or unable to accede to the Bearer’s implicit request may signal this with #76, #77, #193 or a disbelieving #111. A condemnatory #36 or #101 serves to express disenchantment with the Bearer in no uncertain terms.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: WTF?
body:
A particularly eloquent means of articulating speechlessness at the stupidity, randomness or simple incomprehensibility of a communication, situation or proposition.

Responses can range from the apologetic #27, the reassuring #117 or #140, to a potentially flustered #185 and mock-accidental #174. Potentially problematic situations can be signalled with #127, but a manic #131 offers perhaps the most effective retort.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "What is this I don't even" (5.1)

title: It's not you, it's me
body: Sometimes a Bearer’s own situation precludes involvement, or prevents them from being able to give another quite what they would like; this message provides eloquent means of articulating such a conflict. Receivers wishing to appeal the Bearer’s decision can send #87, #44 or #33 to beg them to reconsider, or #95 to disagree with their statement; #69 queries the potentially saddening results of receiving such a missive. Those wishing to acquiesce with understanding and courtesy have #53 or #137 with which to do so (or, if they wish to be somewhat more flippant, #122). Should declaring the Receiver’s own feelings be paramount, #57 or #152 offer romantically intense - if perhaps unwise - means of expression. #127 acknowledges the awkwardness of the situation, whereas #98 and #111 expresses shock at a sudden announcement.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Surprise me
body: A challenge, a tease and a gesture of trust - #100 is all three. A Bearer may be testing the Receiver’s mettle, wishing to understand them better, or simply be seeking excitement or interesting experiences with a valued companion; the precise nature of such experiences, of course, is limited only by the Receiver’s imagination. Responses can vary from the confident #96 to the sinister #131. Of course, #100 can also be sent as an ironic response to some declaration of the Receiver’s - perhaps #72, or #77? - as well as deflating somewhat the self-conscious #131.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Make it stop
body:
Fingernails down a blackboard, misplaced apostrophes, ridiculous workloads - an affectionate if tongue-in-cheek plea from the Bearer to make it all go away, now, please. Preferably yesterday. And a cup of tea would be nice.

Receivers sympathetic to the Bearer’s plight can indicate the fact with #84 and offer support with #55; encouragement can be sent with #83, #158 or #117. Those willing to accede to the Bearer’s request can do so with #70, those unable to with #182, while conditions can be imposed with #94 or a refusal given in #67. #195 promises compensation for whatever iniquity prompted the Bearer’s desperation, but whether such a gesture is adequate only the parties concerned can decide.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Creep
body:
