A resounding dismissal, with explicit overtones of personal insult missing from the more offhand #25. Perhaps the Bearer considers the Receiver weird, or not to belong. Not a message to be sent without good reason, perhaps, but particularly effective in expressing disparagement of the Receiver.

Those wishing to respond with disdain can use #180, or #30 to open hostilities, while #176 admits defeat and #48 informs the Receiver a grave mistake has occurred. Should a Receiver wish to engage further with the Bearer, #69, #149 or #12 offer opportunity for this, albeit at the risk of possibly proving the Bearer right…
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Body cites #150, which is not an entry in any source (unresolved also in the April 2013 book layout).

title: You're not my type
body: Whilst the Bearer may think highly of the Receiver, they simply do not wish for romantic closeness to them; whether for reasons of physical allure, emotional incompatibility, or simply a disjunction in beliefs or values. Whilst this is a difficult decision to appeal, based as it is on the Bearer’s very personal desires, #168 implores them to reconsider, and #41 suggests the Receiver will wait until they do; #87 promises them anything in return for a chance, and #44 acknowledges that this may be the last possible opportunity to connect. Should the Receiver wish merely to express their anguish, #146 enables them to do so. It is often wiser to accept such decisions gracefully, though, as with #154, #137 or #161.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Anything once
body:
Well, why not, indeed? Whilst quite possibly unsure of the possible outcomes of a Receiver’s plans or intentions, whether expressed florally or otherwise, this Bearer is more than willing to give their suggestion a shot.

Used as frequently to respond to #56 as to the more personal implications of #5, #1 or even #138, #105 is a light-hearted and sometimes brave means of expressing willingness to move outside one’s comfort zone. Responses depend on the nature of the suggested plan: #157 or #134 express simple joy in the Bearer, while #131 teasingly implies evil intent, and #180 points out the Receiver’s feelings may differ substantially from those of the Bearer. #140 highlights the trust between parties, and #128 and #93 express possible reasons for demurring.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Perfect
body:
For this Bearer, neither the Receiver nor any aspect of their time together could possibly be improved upon. Communicating joy in the present and hope for the future, this is perhaps as lovely to send as to receive.

In exchange #19, #34, #59, #152 declare a passionate romantic bond, while #46 and #47 communicate trust and possession. #118 declares (hopefully joyful!) surprise at the turn matters have taken, while #87 indicates unconditional surrender to the Bearer’s love and #62 demands playful assurance of their feelings. Should the implied adoration be impractical for some reason, #95 expresses yearning, and #114 a serious and potentially unpleasant conversation on the horizon.

In the rare circumstances where such a communication is unwelcome, #65 and #71 express hesitation, #95 a potentially futile yearning; while #144, #63, #98, or #22 may perhaps give some indication as to why.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I dare you
body: Wisely or otherwise, thus speaks a Bearer determined to challenge, provoke and perhaps entice a Receiver. The dare in question could be anything from flirtatious suggestion to improbable and impractical physical idiocy; whether the Receiver feels able to refuse such an eloquent proposition, whatever its foolishness, is another matter entirely. Should they wish to do so, #111 indicates disbelief, #71 reluctance, and #51 the certainty that anything else would be preferable to whatever the Bearer is daring. #6, #70 and #87 show willingness, and #86 the conviction that the Receiver is eminently capable of surviving whatever the Bearer can throw at them. Those wishing to communicate horror, stress or distress, however, have #78 at their disposal.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: That was... interesting
body:
Some experiences, particularly unexpected ones, are definitely preferable in retrospect - but one hopes there is some sort of lesson to be learned from most things. Such a message acknowledges the difficult or troubling nature of something Bearer and Receiver have shared, be it a meeting, a holiday, an event or a party, but unites the pair in their wry appreciation of its cessation.

Receivers genuinely appreciative of the experience in question can use #45, while #23 and #105 acknowledge that such things happen, and #161 suggests that the knowledge gained might be worth it. #149 expresses regret, #159 the lack thereof, and #69 asks whether whatever has happened will have dire consequences. #183 swears never to repeat the experience, #195 promises to make amends, and #186 suggests the mutual assertion that Nothing. Ever. Happened.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You've gotta be kidding me
body: Utter disbelief is expressed here; what on earth was the Receiver talking about? Cheeky Receivers can excuse potentially transgressive behaviour with #161, dare the Bearer to acquiesce with #107 and maintain a mysterious or threatening demeanour with #131; criticise the Bearer’s dramatic tones with #184; plead necessity with #182 or beg forgiveness with #113. A forlorn #95 or wheedling #168 implore the Bearer to reconsider.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "You gotta be kidding me *" (Code Generator)

title: Forgive me
body: However difficult, this Bearer accepts responsibility for past mistakes or damaging consequences, and pleads with the Receiver to accept their profound regret and apology. Depending on the magnitude of the Bearer’s offence, replies can be as simple as #81 or #148, or as specific as #94 or #44. #114 invites discussion, if painfully so. Should the Receiver wish to refuse the Bearer’s plea, a pointed #193, critical #48, disbelieving #111, unequivocal #36 or sardonic #180 all offer variously cutting means of doing so.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: We need to talk
body: A seemingly innocuous request, with forbidding overtones indeed. Perhaps unfortunately, such a communication has been long held to herald some drastic change in any connection - if not a parting of ways, some serious news. Any Receiver of such a message would be entirely justified in sending a swift #69, in the hopes of receiving #57 or #34 in response. Sometimes, however, #51, #72 or #63 may be directly relevant - although #159 adds a positive if consolatory note. #194 asks about possible slips by the Receiver, #167 directly enquires as to the nature of a Bearer’s concerns, and #178 offers tongue-in-cheek acknowledgement of the situation’s gravity. Receivers anxious to make their feelings known can send #152, while #22 suggests the Bearer is deceived somewhat, #33 asks for respite; #44 makes it clear matters are reaching crisis point; and a simple #128 suggests an entirely reasonable note of fear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Code Generator.xlsx (Jan 2013) gives code 11122, CSV gives 2233. Earlier titles: "We have to talk" (5.1, 5.4, 5.5, Code Generator)

title: I miss you
body: Without the Receiver’s company, this Bearer’s world is just a little emptier, sadder, colder. Whether their separation is the temporary result of circumstance or the permanence of parting, this Bearer needs the Receiver to know how much their absence matters. Sometimes #34 or #57 is the best means of communicating comfort and reassurance, but the intensity of desire in #19, #4 and #130 may also reflect the Receiver’s feelings. #46 reinforces the mutuality of possession and commitment. #87 affirms the Receiver’s intention of going to any lengths in pleasing the Bearer. #62 invites them to prove the truth of their feelings, whilst in less happy circumstances #60 or #67 may be necessary to clarify a difficult situation. An ironic #192 offers a potentially inflammatory counter to the Bearer’s sentiments.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You've changed
body: A statement often saddened and saddening; a Bearer is under the impression that something has changed, for better or worse, in their relationship with the Receiver. #22 directly contradicts the Bearer, but whether or not this is wise is a moot point. #53 signals understanding, while requesting further detail with #194 or #80 often assists in clarifying matters. Sometimes a response to #118, #116 can be answered with a simple, if taciturn, #73 or #74, or expanded upon with #69. #163 proclaims innocence, while #23 acknowledges the Bearer’s truth but points out its inevitability; #87 promises anything to make the Receiver feel better, while #171 asks whether changes are in fact mutual.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Keep calm & carry on
body: The floral equivalent of a cup of tea, this proffers encouragement to a Receiver stressed, troubled or beset by the demands of profession or circumstance, from a Bearer confident in their capabilities and wishing to show faith. Of course, if the Receiver is that busy, reply of any kind may be wishful thinking. However, should opportunity arise, #121 or #134 express gratitude; #115 or #130 desire for the Bearer, and #86 the assurance that Receiver too is confident in their ability to prevail. #183 refuses the Bearer outright; #41 declares the Receiver’s willingness to give the Bearer what time they need; #122 implicitly repudiates their concern; #101 begs them to make it go away, and #159 declares the Receiver’s acceptance of the negative consequences of their decision.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Keep calm & carry on/don’t give up" (5.1)

title: What's happened to us?
body:
Somewhere, Bearer and Receiver have become lost to one another; this Bearer seeks explanation, understanding, a healing of the breach. Both an appeal to address the problem and a nostalgic plea to recall good times gone before the chance of redemption is lost forever, #118 is rarely less than heartfelt.

A Receiver wishing to reassure the Bearer of their commitment despite the distance between them can reply with #57, #46 or #66.

Those feeling a state of disrepair fundamentally the responsibility of the Bearer can communicate this with #116, #149 and #146 means of expressing emotional responses.

#101 or #33 constitute appeals to rectify matters, but should the situation be irretrievable, #154, #99, or #63 all offer explanations and more-or-less gentle refusals. #114 invites the Bearer to discuss matters in somewhat sombre tones, while #83 reassures them that whatever’s happening does not necessarily mean the end of all that is between them.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Get well soon
body: Succour and sympathy to a Receiver ill or in distress. Obviously immediate response is by no means required, but a retrospective #121 rarely goes amiss; or #115 or #134 if appropriate for the parties concerned. Receivers wishing simply to cheer themselves up can reply with a playful #101, or #78, although if the Bearer’s sympathies were unwelcome a well-placed #103 or #169 makes the point clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: More
body:
Not only can this Bearer take whatever the Receiver has in mind, but it’s by no means enough, and they wish the Receiver to increase their attentions. Prospective Bearers are advised to be quite certain before sending, however, lest they receive somewhat in excess of what they bargained for.

Appreciative Receivers can respond with #87, #6 or #46; the reluctant, however, have #26, #76 or #111 with which to make the point, and in all cases #91 may serve as a timely reminder.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Thank you
body: A simple offer of thanks for some gesture, compliment or gift given by Receiver to Bearer. Courteous, polite, and often highly significant to receive, #121 can be greeted with anything from the playful self-deprecation of #163 to the equally mannered #151, and everything in between.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Whatever
body: Studiedly noncommittal, this Bearer is particularly concerned the Receiver is aware of their disinterest in the matter at hand. It’s all the same to them. Particularly irksome in response to an emotional enquiry or specific request, irate Receivers may wish to consider sending #36, #144 or #30 to make their feelings clear. #48 declares the Bearer committing a cardinal error, #195 promises and irate Bearer redress, and #35 demands appropriate honesty, at the very least.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You're beautiful
body:
Beauty is arresting, touching, eternal and earthly at once; lost somewhere between terror, solace, salvation and loss. Such a simple compliment, and yet one so central to so many human passions. Whether from an unexpected stranger, newfound lover or beloved partner, the absolute sincerity of such appreciation is rarely unwelcome, often disarming and sometimes powerfully affecting.

For those positively inclined, a simple #13 or #34 may suffice in reply, while #130 make the Receiver’s feelings clear. #95 or #193 disclaim the compliment, while #121 accepts it with grace. Should the parties be insufficiently acquainted, #31 or #153 enable delicate enquiries to be made, while #5 anticipates an enjoyable connection.

#46 and #47, on the other hand, make undertones of romantic possession clear.

In the unlikely event a Receiver wishes to reject both the Bearer’s statement and their advances, a dismissive #122 provides quite definitive indication of the fact.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Body cites #32, which is not an entry in any source (unresolved also in the April 2013 book layout).

title: About time
body: This Bearer has been waiting some time for events to unfold, or for the Receiver to reach a particular conclusion - and wishes to mark the culmination of their long-held anticipation. Receivers sharing both their perspective and their appreciation can concur with #157, whilst any feeling personally criticised for unwished delay can playfully refute the Bearer’s implicit accusation with #163 or #122. #195 promises recompense, #60 offers a playful reprimand, while #151 asserts - however spuriously - any delay was enjoyable to the Receiver.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Maybe
body: So much still to consider! Unwilling to commit as yet to any particular decision, the matter under discussion is still one of significance to the Bearer, and to answer with such ambiguity is to invite further discussion. #143, #114, or #12 are often useful for this purpose, depending on the gravity of the situation; particularly understanding Receivers can offer assistance with #89 or request instructions with #97, whereas those rapidly losing patience with the Bearer can communicate this with #44, #98 or #124. Should the Bearer’s uncertainty mark a shift in the relationship, #116 or #118 make this explicit, and #69 requests reassurance for the future.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Enjoy
body: Light-hearted and comfortable, affectionate farewell or simply encouragement about a Receiver’s daily business, #126 offers the Bearer’s blessing and good wishes. Sent as part of a dialogue, it can mean either loving reassurance of the Bearer’s appreciation of the Receiver’s independent life and activities, or a companionable highfive between friends. #95 (or a sarcastic #86) suggest the Receiver finds the possibility of such enjoyment unlikely at best. #24 begs for assistance; #78 or #128 emote fear or panic; and #54 indicates the Receiver regards the Bearer’s message as suspicious at best. Whilst #126 often closes a dialogue, #81, #94 and #105 all offer further detail, and #4 makes the centrality of the Receiver to such an eventuality strikingly clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Awkward
body:
Someone is unwittingly doing something which makes life potentially uncomfortable for all parties. That someone, Receiver, may be you.

Should this be the case, #185 and #137 acknowledge culpability, and #176 metaphorically flings both hands in the air. #27 apologises, #174 suggests the Bearer is mistaken, and #186 suggests both parties pretend nothing has happened. Receivers puzzled by receipt of #127 can express the fact with a direct #98, deny caring with #122, and evoke the intensity of their feelings with #78. #195 promises reparation, #126 cheekily instructs the Bearer to relish the experience, and #140 begs for further trust, however futile that may turn out to be.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Fear
body: This Bearer is afraid, whether of the Receiver’s possible actions or of an ongoing situation relevant to both. Whether the Receiver is personally responsible for the Bearer’s state of mind or not, #55 or #89 enquire as to whether any help can be given and reassure the Bearer of the Receiver’s continued presence. Should the Receiver have intentionally prompted terror, of course, #162 says so explicitly and #131 or #48 may be appropriate, whilst #140 suggests trust in the Receiver can counter the Bearer’s concerns. #117 offers universal support, #195 promises to make amends, while #80 asks for further detail and #83 counsels endurance. #192 offers sympathy laconic at best, and #184 none whatsoever.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I want you
body: An intense, wordless, breathless longing beating behind everyday life, speaking of the press and slide of skin and bone and weight and warmth, muscle and fingers and mouth; this Bearer wants the Receiver beyond sense or reason. #152, #19, #4 or #59 are all equally ardent responses, although a simple #34 or the passionate possession of #46 and #47 may be preferred. Confident Receivers may send the demanding #62, while those wishing only to surrender to the Bearer may do so with #86, #87 or #120. #123, with its simple appreciation of the Bearer’s beauty, is also often a worthy response. #42 expresses the Receiver’s anticipation of future meetings, while #60 counsels patience, and #3 dispenses with the need for it. Should the Bearer’s desire not be reciprocated, #22, #49, #67, or #71 make this clear, while #104, #63, or #154 offer explanations and #127, #101 or #103 make the impossibility of any future connection quite clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Desire" (5.1)

title: Evil laugh
body:
Mwwahahahaahhaha! Mmwahahahahahaha! MwahahahahahahahahHAHAHAHAH! MWAHAHAHAHAHA! MWAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!!!

Receivers struggling for responses may find #98, #78, #103, #178, #30 or #163 helpful.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Good luck
body: For Receivers about to embark on some venture, #132 offers support, encouragement and an appeal to Fortune to look kindly upon their endeavours. Rooting wholeheartedly for the Bearer, #132 is a simple gesture of goodwill and care. Responding may be as easy as #121 or #134, but Receivers may also wish to express their feelings about an upcoming event with #128, #78 or #157, or reinforce their relationship with the Receiver with #34, #152, or #115. #183 declares the emphatic intent to avoid all related situations in future. Receivers troubled about upcoming possibilities can plead for help with #24 or #101, although whether Bearers will be in any position to assist is somewhat of a moot point.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You rock!
body: This Bearer’s world is a better place because the Receiver is in it. Whether with companionship, compassion, cake or comfort, the Receiver provides inspiration, affection or succour to a Bearer wishing to make their gratitude and appreciation known. #170 echoes their sentiment with a teasing edge, while #121 thanks them for their recognition, and #95 or #38 express their perceived unworthiness of the sentiment. The promised support of #55, the affectionate devotion of #46 or the slightly smug edge of #162 may also be appropriate.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Fair enough
body: This Bearer accepts the Receiver’s position, whatever it may be, with a shrug of the shoulders. Grateful Receivers can use #134, #190 or #121 to thank them, or #146 or #149 to regret the emotional consequences of their decision. If said decision appears inexplicable to the Bearer, #80 or #143 can be used to request further information.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You shouldn't have done that
body: Somehow, matters have not gone according to plan; perhaps conflict, pain or confusion have resulted from a supposedly light-hearted reunion or casual gift, the Receiver has created some public misunderstanding at the Bearer’s expense, or the parties have been deceived or at odds in their feelings for one another. #138 enables the Bearer to make this quite clear, and re-establish their relationship on a more honest, if sadder, footing. Receivers concurring with the Bearer’s assessment can accept responsibility and apologise with #27, or beg forgiveness with #113, while #174 maintains the Bearer is not in full possession of the facts and thus their criticism is unjustified. #140 suggests the Bearer’s judgement is premature, #114 or #53 offer explanations, and #17 bemoans the implacability of fate. #44 makes it clear that matters are at breaking point, while a cheeky #161 or #163 lighten the tone.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "You shouldn't've done that" (5.1, 5.4, 5.5, Code Generator)

title: Thinking of you
body: This Bearer has the Receiver on their mind - whether because the latter is going through difficulties, the pair have a newfound or changing connection, or simply share long-held closeness. #171 asserts the mutuality of such consideration, #115 laments the Bearer’s absence, #60 implicitly promises future unity, while #5 and #96 suggest a meeting and #134 expresses a friendly appreciation of the Bearer’s sentiments.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Trust me
body: Such a message suggests the Receiver place their absolute trust in the Bearer; easily asked, perhaps, but for many a difficult leap of faith. Whether in regard to a specific plan or promise, or simply as encouragement to or reinforcement of further intimacy, #140 is a significant and powerful gesture, not to be undertaken lightly. Categoric refusal is offered by #54, and those wishing for absolute honesty beforehand have #35 with which to insist. Those willing to do as the Bearer asks - or already in a position to do so - can send #18, but any wishing to advise caution can send #11, and those with reason to doubt #44. Fear or anger at the Bearer’s request are expressed in #128 or #144, whilst Receivers wishing to make the degree of their faith in the Bearer emphatically clear have #46 and #87 at their disposal.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Trust me/I promise?" (5.1, 5.4, 5.5)

title: Penny for your thoughts?
body: Less intense than #167, this is a simple enquiry as to what’s on the Receiver’s mind. Perhaps they’ve appeared troubled, distracted or fraught, or perhaps the Bearer simply feels distanced from them in some sense and wishes to reconnect. Receivers who have no wish to confide can use an unequivocal #39, a brisk #37 or a sharp #175 to make this clear; those thinking in some way of the Bearer can say so with #139, an appreciative #123 or a passionate #19; while sadness is evident in #146, anger in #144 and happiness in #157.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: How could you?
body:
The burning, pounding, incisive anger carried with this message imply a Bearer betrayed, disrespected, hurt or deeply frustrated. Whatever the Receiver has done, the Bearer is furious, and seeks recognition and reparation.

Should the parties involved be content with resolution through conflict, #30 makes matters blisteringly clear; should Receivers seek forgiveness, however, they may use #113 to do so. #174 suggests mistake on the part of the Bearer. #185 offers a tongue-in-cheek acknowledgement of offence received, while #159 asserts that the Receiver considers their actions entirely worth it and #161 implies that it was at least worth trying. #69 or #44 seek to resolve conflict with the Bearer and promise strenuous effort to do so, while Receivers gravely troubled by the impact of their actions on the Bearer can apologise with #27 or suggest their own emotional turmoil with #146 or #149. #87 makes it emphatically clear that the Receiver will do anything to mitigate the Bearer’s rage, but such extravagant gestures should perhaps be made with caution.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Jealousy
body: Here is a Bearer consumed with the insidious, frantic passion of jealousy, with all its echoes of inadequacy, despondency and loss. Whilst a Bearer may be seeking clarification, reassurance or simply expression, a Receiver can offer confirmation with #72, disbelief with #111 or passionate rebuttal with #46, #66, #181, or #4. Those wishing to communicate only their own emotional states in response have #146, or #27 to offer a simple, heartfelt apology, while #113 begs forgiveness for a transgression accurately perceived. #22 declares the Bearer a victim of their own overactive imagination; #77 asserts the complexity of the situation; #174 the Bearer’s mistake; #184 implies the Bearer is overreacting, while #195 promises redress and #186 proposes, however impractically, that both parties forget whatever prompted the Bearer’s concern.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Despair
body: Every breath is a body blow; this Bearer has lost everything, hope most of all. They want to give up, seeing no way out of whatever situation is causing their pain, and wish only that the Receiver know this. Whilst such a message is often hard to respond to, #27 offers apologies for any personal responsibility, and #113 implores forgiveness. #132 and #84 offer sympathy and wish the Bearer luck, while #23 and #117 counsel resignation and acceptance. For lovers anxious to reinforce their relationship amid the chaos #57 enable them to do so. #89 offers practical help, whereas those able to offer only long-distance support can do so with #139. Should the Receiver consider the Bearer unnecessarily melodramatic, #192 undercuts them beautifully, while #165 decries their immaturity and #169 and #184 dismiss them as annoying.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Code Generator.xlsx (Jan 2013) gives code 2445, CSV gives 1334. Code 1334 is shared by #146 Despair and #162 My work here is done in messages.csv; Code Generator gives 2445 for #146 (2445 is otherwise unused).

title: Congratulations
body: Joy for the Receiver’s achievement bubbles out of such a message, whether sent to honour artistic achievement, professional success, a new arrival, such an auspicious occasion as engagement or marriage, or just the successful negotiation of difficulties in the Receiver’s life. Whilst classic responses like #121 and #134 express gratitude and appreciation of the Bearer’s gesture, an opportunity for further intimacy can be created with #123, #5 or #6, or decided (if discourteous) rejection of the Bearer with #103 or #37.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I forgive you
body: Whatever crime has been committed or mistake made by the Receiver, the Bearer is willing to forgive. A gracious and often loving gesture, it is usually churlish to reply with hostility. Grateful Receivers may send #121, or #34, #152 or #4 to lovers; those feeling themselves unworthy of the Bearer’s magnanimity can assert the fact with #38, or use #198 to acknowledge the generosity of such a gesture. Those doubting the Bearer’s word can point this out with #54, and beg for an honest assessment of the situation with #35. Should the Receiver feel innocent of any wrongdoing, a swift #188 may be sent. #163 maintains a potentially spurious innocence, while #124 roundly asserts that such an admission is long overdue. #98 declares complete bafflement, or (potentially) denial.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Regret
body:
A Bearer haunted by the echoes of things done or undone, spoken or unspoken, found or lost, wishes at least to make their awareness of lost possibilities or passions known. Whether longing to rectify the situation or simply to express sorrow for pain caused, this Bearer recognises and accepts the consequences of their actions, however mistaken they may have been.

Forgiveness can be offered explicitly with #148, and more playfully with #179. #23 acknowledges ongoing complexity, and implicitly shifts responsibility from the Bearer onto the general mess of human emotional life; #62 demands restitution; #44 offers one last chance; and #57 assures the Bearer of the Receiver’s ultimate devotion. Receivers wishing to blank the incident from the record can propose doing so with #186, and those determined never to repeat whichever experience prompted the exchange can articulate this with #183. #20 reprimands the Bearer for not heeding the Receiver’s advice; #35 demands the Bearer tell the truth about their actions, feelings or behaviour; #118 laments the effect of the Bearer’s behaviour on their relationship; and #100 ironically accepts the truth of the expressed sentiment. #192 offers potentially ironic sympathy, and #173 offers the similarly laconic wish for improved outcome in the future.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: April 2013 book layout text differs (similarity 0.908; mainly layout trims/reference formatting).

title: My pleasure
body: Such a message declares that whatever services the Bearer has performed for the Receiver, they were not only happy to do so but positively relished the experience. Often a response to #121, #151 is also relevant to #107, #120 or #62. Appropriate responses are often anticipatory (#41 or #42), teasing (#87 or #120) or emotional #134 or #38.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I need you
body: This Bearer is lost without the Receiver; lost within them, lost where they are not. The intensity of such a message is echoed in #4, the passionate assertion that only the Bearer matters; #46 and #47 reinforce the couple’s possession of each other, while #66 declares lifelong commitment. #34 and #130 articulate romantic longing and affirmation, while #19 reflects the edge of desperation in the Bearer’s message, and #62 asks the Bearer to somehow prove the truth of their love. #87 promises the Bearer whatever they desire, while #106 asserts their perfection and #139 assures them of a place at the forefront of the Receiver’s mind. #158 and #55 offer support whilst lightening the tone decidedly. Should the Receiver be less comfortable with the intensity of the Bearer’s feelings, they can advise caution with #11 or #65, imply panic with #24 or cynicism with #192, or (worst of all) dismiss the Bearer with #111 or even #122. However, it is wise to consider carefully before doing so, because such gestures are often irrevocable.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Do you feel the same?
body: Whatever the emotions swimming between Bearer and Receiver, this Bearer is anxious to know whether they are shared. Perhaps the Bearer has made a confession of love or desire, and as yet the Receiver has made no response; possibly Bearer and Receiver have just met, but the Bearer is uncertain of the Receiver’s interest or lack thereof; possibly something has changed in their relationship and Bearer is anxious to see whether newfound feelings are mutual. #83 or a more specific #1 offer encouragement to the Bearer, and #61 suggests the dawn of a new era between the parties. Often sent as followup when some communication has been met with silence, Receivers can let the Bearer down gently with #17, #63, #104 or #67, or somewhat harshly with #111, #22, or the unequivocal #103.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Let's be friends
body:
A versatile gesture equally appropriate inviting a newfound acquaintance to further intimacy, or orchestrating the sad cessation of a formerly romantic connection. In either case, of course, the care inherent in the beauty of the gift may perhaps serve to declare ongoing interest in the wellbeing of the Receiver, at the very least.

Receivers welcoming the chance of a new comrade can do so with an enthusiastic #134 or #157, a milder #189, or reject such an invitation with a terse #188, a compensatory #173 or a cheeky #181. Those devastated at the loss of a partner, however, can express their sorrow with #146 or #178, plead for another chance with #44 or #168, declare themselves well pleased with the outcome with #190, or dismiss potential pain with #192. More sensitively, however, a #161 or #159 at least indicate the relationship was worth it.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Squee
body:
Thus speaks a Bearer jubilantly appreciative, either of the Receiver's virtues or of the outcome of events in which both are involved. A simple expression of joy, to receive #157 is at face value nothing but a pleasure. Should it be received under unpleasant circumstances, however, such glee takes on a barbed air of schadenfreude, and should be used with care.

Receivers concurring with the Bearer's delight can do so with #171 or #106, or express detached appreciation of their enthusiasm with #196 or #134. In less harmonious circumstances, #178 or #30 open hostilities; while Receivers wishing to dismiss the Bearer's sentiments can do so with #122, or a more critical #103.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Cheer up
body: Worse things happen at sea. Possibly things with tentacles. This Bearer has noticed a Receiver’s sadness, and wishes to make them smile; the equivalent of cake, tea and sympathy, or possibly a Blackadder box set. Appreciative Receivers can send #121 or #134 in thanks, or #78 or #101 to relieve their feelings. The romantic can warn of particular vulnerabilities in their current mindset with #11, or reaffirm their trust in the Bearer with #18; in some cases, a simple #1 will suffice. #86 asserts the ability to cope fine, thank you very much, while #37 suits those who feel the Bearer’s attentions inappropriate.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: No regrets
body:
Whatever’s happened, this Bearer would do it all again. The pleasure was worth the pain, the joy the loss; some lessons will always be worth the price. Sent to a newfound lover as part of an ongoing courtship, it reinforces the Bearer’s satisfaction with current events and their dedication to pursuing the path already embarked upon with the Receiver; arriving after a parting of the ways, it nevertheless declares in no uncertain terms that the Bearer is glad to have shared themselves and their life with the Receiver, however briefly.

As part of an ongoing dialogue, perhaps a defiant response to #138 or a tender acknowledgement of #118, it serves to make the Bearer’s position unequivocally clear. If the parties are romantically involved or new to one another, responding with #13, #59, #45 or #106 makes mutual appreciation clear; should they have recently parted, #146 or #149 all express the Receiver’s sadness. #140 or #198 may also be useful in bringing the parties closer together.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Don't make promises you can't keep
body:
A wry warning to a Receiver whose promises – whether of time, thought or action - repeatedly outstrip their performance. Whilst not angry as such, this Bearer certainly wishes to make their awareness of the discrepancy clear – and urge the Receiver to be more honest in future.

Of course, appropriate responses depend entirely upon the circumstances occasioning the Receiver’s unsatisfactory behaviour. Should pressing but imminently resolvable matters be the cause, #60 should suffice to make positions clear; #140 urges the Receiver to have faith in the Bearer, or #44 begs for one last chance. Should a Receiver wish to make amends, #87 or #27 indicate this, and #97 asks for suggestions; #94 imposes conditions, #62 turns the Bearer’s criticism on its head, while Receivers wishing to challenge the Bearer have #111 or #22 with which to do so.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Worth a shot
body:
Perhaps the outcome of this Bearer’s actions was not quite what they’d anticipated or hoped, but nevertheless, they are glad to have made the attempt; or perhaps they wish to urge the Receiver that a potential risk is worth it. Recognising that intent and outcome are rarely coincident, both Bearers consider that, on balance, lessons learned can be worth the price; #161 can, in fact, be a particularly encouraging message.

Receivers who have in some sense paid for the Bearer’s actions or fear doing so can make criticism clear with #138, #103 or #111, or more generously offer forgiveness with #148. Those wishing to distance themselves from the Bearer can do so emphatically with #25, or dismissively with #122. Any feeling the exchange premature for some reason can use #83 to indicate the fact, while #81 or #159 echo their sentiments and #173 offers gentle encouragement.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Worth a shot (duplicate 159 ‘no regrets’?)" (5.1)

title: My work here is done
body: This Bearer is entirely and possibly a little smugly (or ironically) satisfied with the outcome of a situation and their personal contribution to it. Receivers somewhat dismayed at such an assertion can communicate a raised eyebrow with #95 or #124, whereas those wishing to playfully encourage the Bearer have #86 or #120 with which to do so. #126 introduces a potentially ironic note into proceedings, whereas if the Bearer’s assertion is valid #137 and #121 offer courteous acknowledgement.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Code 1334 is shared by #146 Despair and #162 My work here is done in messages.csv; Code Generator gives 2445 for #146 (2445 is otherwise unused).

title: Who, me?
body: The voice of possibly spurious innocence, #163 is often used in primarily silly or hostile exchanges, although it is also relevant in response to serious messages like #116, semi-serious ones such as #12, #47, #160 or #138. Replies are heavily dependent on the tone of the original communication; #73, #111, and #165 all imply flippancy and friendliness, while #193 offers sarcastic denial, and #44 introduces a serious note.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Grow up
body: This Bearer is dismayed at the Receiver’s apparent immaturity, whether in matters of the heart or simply as a result of regular exposure to their conduct in daily life. Particularly powerful in the latter circumstance if sent anonymously, it can be countered with a patronising #167, a smug #162, a spuriously innocent #163, a triumphantly incomprehensible #78 or a defiant #98. An ironic #67 or #151 is almost guaranteed to infuriate the Bearer, although whether or not this serves to prove their point is a matter worthy of consideration. A cutting #103, threatening #30 or critical #48 all not only criticise the Bearer’s judgement but suggest the possibility of dire consequences; an end also achievable through judicious deployment of #131.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: What's troubling you?
body: A Receiver has become cold and distant, for no reason the Bearer can fathom; perhaps they are even openly dismissive without any explanation. #167 constitutes a plea, for explanation at the very least, but preferably with reconciliation in mind. Receivers unaware of any change in behaviour but anxious to reassure the Bearer can declare their feelings with #1, #34, or #4, or acknowledge difficulties with #114 or a mournful #118. Those who have indeed been upset by the Bearer – or by something else – can express the problem with #145, #54, #72, #138, or #63, while those doubting the Bearer’s word have #35 or #80 with which to request further discussion. Warnings of upcoming or potential emotional havoc can be given with #11, #93 or #144, and Bearers would be well advised to heed such concerns.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Have I upset you? [something I said?]" (5.1)

title: Please
body: Whether sent as a request in itself, on the assumption the Receiver will be well aware of precisely what the Bearer desires, or as a response to rejection or refusal from the Receiver, this is a powerful and often intimate appeal for (re)consideration. Whether an appeal for clemency (perhaps in response to #67 or #63), a statement of enthusiasm for #5, #3, or #96, or even a fervent acquiescence to #89, replies can be as simple as #73 or #74, as intensely inviting as #47 or #151, as equivocal as #76, #77 or #65, as insulting as #103 or as (supposedly) determined as #181. A sardonic #193, devoted #191 or intriguing #195 may also offer means of developing a delicate relationship between Bearer and Receiver.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You dent my calm
body: The Receiver has been getting on the Bearer’s nerves, whether with annoying habits, unfortunate behaviour, or simply inconvenient emotion, and the Bearer wishes none-too-gently to point out the fact. Abashed Receivers can apologise with #27 or #113, but may also wish to convey blank incomprehension with #98, or send a defiant #162 or #163. #26 advises the Bearer of their foolishness, #148 proffers forgiveness in the face of the insult, #125 suggests potential recognition that the Bearer has a point, while #194 enquires mildly as to the nature of such irritation. Should receipt of such a message mark the emergence of serious issues between the parties – or a Receiver wish to maintain a detached and ironic tone – #69 may be sent, although it’s always wise to bear in mind the answer may well be #177, or even #36.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "You’re irritating" (5.1, 5.4, 5.5); "You're irritating" (Code Generator)

title: You'll do
body: An affectionate, if tongue-in-cheek and occasionally somewhat wounding, means of expressing satisfaction with or appreciation of a Receiver; often one whose own emotions are somewhat more unequivocally expressed. Particularly useful in undercutting the self-deprecation of #38, responding can often be tricky; #122 is offhand and flippant, #151 courteous, #20 defiant, #121 teasing, while #131 or #180 somewhat undermine the Bearer’s assumption of superiority. Should such a message arrive out of the blue, however, Receivers would be quite justified in sending #98, #36 or a mock-innocent #163 in reply.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Likewise
body: This Bearer wishes to echo the Receiver's sentiments in every particular. Usually an expression of accord, whether in harmony or disharmony, #171 can be as useful as an affirmation (to #134 or #34 for example) or as a warning (in response to #145, #30 or #138). It can be polite (sent in acknowledgement of #187) or critical (a comeback to #160 or #54). Responses evidently vary according to the tone of the exchange, but #114, #131, #144, #69, #78 or #122 may all be useful.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Admit it
body: This Bearer is frustrated by the Receiver’s inability to acknowledge what they consider a self-evident truth. Particularly poignant in situations where the Bearer feels mutual attraction is unacknowledged or that the Receiver is deliberately deceiving them, a simple #1, #197 or #72 can be used to clear matters up – albeit not always to the Bearer’s satisfaction. #80 begs for more information, #114 requests crisis talks, while #118 and #116 lament changes in the relationship between Bearer and Receiver, and #98 or #111 articulate incomprehension. Receivers can suggest misunderstanding with #174, #49 or #48, while #140 begs for trust and #43 concedes defeat. Should such a demand be inappropriate, #37 or #103 makes the point quite clearly.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Better luck next time
body: Matters may have gone awry, but this Bearer hopes that things will be different next time around. Receivers appreciative of such support can indicate the fact with #134, while those doubting the Bearer’s assurances can say so with #95 and those in inconvenient or uncomfortable circumstances beg for advice or insight with #97 or #35. Despairing Receivers can communicate the fact with #146 or a milder #122, while cynics can make their feelings clear with a sarcastic #168.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: It's not what it looks like
body: It is imperative to this Bearer that the Receiver does not take recent revelations or events at face value. A common response to #144 or #72, #174 begs for at least the chance to explain before any irrevocable actions are taken. Receivers minded to do so can ask for further explanations with #80 or an assertive #114, while those horrified and wishing to make this clear can send an accusatory #144, doubtful #54 or incredulous #98. #118 and #69 ask painful questions about the future of the relationship between Bearer and Receiver; #122 speaks of dismissal, and #148 or #179 potentially magnanimous forgiveness; meanwhile, #111 can be used as a cutting conclusion to any potential dialogue.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "It’s not what it looks" (5.1)

title: You can't handle the truth
body: The Receiver of such a message may have begged the Bearer to tell them everything – with #35 perhaps – but, accurately or otherwise, the Bearer seriously doubts their ability to cope with it. However frustrating this may be for a Receiver who feels themselves better able to judge their capacities than the Bearer, #175 provides ample implication that whatever revelations may be forthcoming are unlikely to be pleasant ones. Any wishing to disabuse the Bearer of notions of their fragility can send #86 to suggest they are categorically mistaken, or #168 to request the Bearer reconsider, while #35 repeats insistences on honesty and #69 indicates continued refusal may have profoundly negative effects. #100 laconically requests the Receiver be allowed to judge their own emotional capacity; #118 laments the need for such discussions in the first place, and #111 asserts in no uncertain terms that the Bearer has severely misjudged.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I give up
body: Such a Bearer is flinging their hands in the air, unwilling or incapable of struggling any longer against seemingly insurmountable forces. Concerned Receivers can urge them to think again with a direct #83, cautious #49 or supportive #55, while #51 declares anything would be preferable to the Receiver than the Bearer’s refusing to continue. A hopeful #173 suggests that whilst surrender may be preferable now, the future may hold other outcomes, whereas hostile Receivers who have been awaiting just such a message can make their feelings known with #124, #52 or a dismissive #122.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "I can’t do this/I give up" (5.1)

title: It's over
body:
Hard to argue with such implacable finality; this Bearer simply wishes it to be known that whatever connection with the Receiver they may have shared in the past, they want no more of it now.

Receivers angry at such dismissal can assert fury with #144, sorrow with #146, indifference with #122, or even a potentially hurtful pleasure with #151, while #118 laments past happiness and #159 makes it clear that the Receiver considers whatever has been shared eminently worth the pain of loss. #51 and #168 beg the Bearer to reconsider, #44 requests one final chance to make things work, while #160 doubts the Bearer’s ability to hold to such a resolution. Should the Receiver also consider such an ending desirable, however, #53 or #137 indicate acceptance of the Bearer’s decision. #36 makes contempt for the Bearer abundantly clear, while #154 suggests simple friendship may be the way forward.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: So it has come to this
body: Dire straits indeed must have brought Bearer and Receiver to such a deadly serious point of conflict. Perhaps the world will never be the same again. Receivers dreading such an eventuality can enquire as to its likelihood with #69, or deny the possibility with #111; #91 or #93 suggest threatening consequences, while #113 pleads for forgiveness and #128 speaks of a Receiver quaking in their metaphorical boots. #118 laments that matters have advanced so far, while #98 denies all knowledge of such tensions and #49 suggests pause for thought may be in order. #131 implies heinous, if currently unknowable, potential outcomes.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Get out of jail free
body: This Bearer is offering the Receiver a consequence-free mistake; to cut them some slack, next time they do something offensive or problematic. Such a gift requires a certain amount of trust in the Receiver not to abuse their licence: an #26 – or even a malevolent #131 - in response suggests such trust might be misplaced, and #67 declares such a gift inappropriate. #121 and #134, however, thank the Bearer. #140 speaks of a Receiver convinced they are unlikely to need such permissions, or prepared to respect limitations, and #46 or #4 suggest the Bearer is all that matters to them in any case. #163 proclaims possibly spurious innocence and #160 doubts their ability to keep their word.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You should be so lucky
body: This Bearer considers that a hubris-ridden Receiver’s ambitions, assertions or desires are overreaching their capacities somewhat. Those confident in their capabilities or their charms can refute such charges with #163, or wryly acquiesce with #100; #161 declares that the venture was worth making in any case, while #140 indicates confidence potentially stemming from knowledge or awareness the Bearer may not in fact possess. #122 dismisses the Bearer’s concerns, #137 acknowledges their validity, while #98 proclaims complete incomprehension and #165 reprimands the Bearer for their tone.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "You shd be so lucky" (5.1)

title: Never
body: Whatever happens to the world or its inhabitants, this Bearer is pretty certain that their mind is made up, unshakeable by faith or reason. Receivers feeling such assurance ill-considered can say so with #26, #48 or #49, while #111 articulates disbelief and #98 confusion. #144 expresses anger at such a conclusion, #146 despair, and #122 dismissal. #168 begs for reconsideration, #44 begs for one last chance, while #36 indicates a Receiver is profoundly unwilling to reopen any sort of negotiation.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: No choice
body: Whatever the Receiver may think, this Bearer sees – or saw – only one way of resolving their difficulties. Whether the result of intrinsic nature or potential consequence, they feel a particular conclusion inevitable. Receivers considering them mistaken can say so with #48 or #49, whilst complications can be suggested with #77 or #95 and reconsideration invited with #168. #137 accepts and agrees with the Bearer’s reasoning, while #111 disbelievingly rejects it and #122 dismisses the question altogether. #144 expresses anger at such an outcome, #146 despair and #145 jealousy, while #148 forgives the Bearer for whatever pain their decision – conscious or otherwise – has caused.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Never again
body: Whatever has happened in the past, this Bearer considers themselves profoundly and permanently unwilling to repeat it. Receivers concurring with such an assessment can say so with #137 or a philosophical #105; any considering any such conclusions irrelevant have #122 with which to say so, while those disagreeing can point out the fact wryly with #95 or incredulously with #111. #107 throws down a challenge, #160 implies a Receiver with little faith in the Bearer’s ability to adhere to their resolution, and #83 constitutes a serious request that the Bearer rethink their certainty.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Get over it
body: Thus speaks a Bearer considerably unimpressed with the perceived melodrama of a Receiver’s reaction to something. Receivers can proclaim their innocence of such histrionics with #163 or their ability to cope with #86, dismiss the Bearer’s implicit insult with #122 or a sarcastic #168, or lament the unlikelihood of such an eventuality with #95. There’s defiance in #151 and rueful acknowledgement in #137, while #116 laments the Bearer’s newfound lack of sympathy. #146 expresses sorrow at the unfolding of events, while #36 articulates the Receiver’s disregard for the Bearer’s perspective in no uncertain terms.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Oops
body: That probably shouldn’t have happened, and this Bearer is apologetically acknowledging the fact. Whether the slip was as dramatic as an accidentally revealed secret or as trivial as a minor catastrophe with the Receiver’s favourite mug, #185 reaches for some sort of shared acknowledgement of mistakes made and hopefully forgiven. #186 concurs, agreeing to forget the incident in question forthwith; #148 forgives the Bearer for whatever damage, physical or emotional, may have been caused, and #91 warns that the consequences of whatever mistake has been made are unlikely to be trauma-free. #138 places responsibility squarely on the Bearer’s shoulders, while #99 does precisely the opposite. #39 announces the intent to keep matters secret. #78 indicates a substantial degree of agitation at the occurrence in question, and #144 blind rage; #44 offers the Bearer one last chance, but it might be wise for Bearers to consider that such gestures are rarely extended more than once.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Let's pretend that never happened
body: Sometimes, it really is preferable to sweep the mess under the rug and start all over again, possibly with a bulldozer, and this Bearer considers their current situation just such a moment. Receivers concurring may do so with a simple #73 or a reflective #109 or #105; those doubting the Bearer’s ability to maintain the promised illusion can say so with #160, and any wishing to assert that it was still worth taking the chance can do so with #161. #94 imposes conditions on the proposed pretence, and #44 makes it clear that this is the last such favour that will be extended, while #179 constitutes assurance of future clemency. #39 promises to keep silent, whilst #131 offers an ominous suggestion of more-or-less orchestrated chaos up ahead. Those unwilling to cooperate with the Bearer’s request can make the fact quite clear with #180, #181 or even #111.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "Let’s pretend that never" (5.1) April 2013 book layout text differs (similarity 0.802; mainly layout trims/reference formatting).

title: Nice to meet you
body: A simple and courteous acknowledgment of pleasure in a new acquaintance. Suitable responses are evidently various depending on the parties concerned and their likely relations. #157 makes it clear such pleasure was mutual, if not magnified. #193 less than politely denies the assertion, and #183 decidedly so. #61 indicates a promising friendship has been established, while colleagues or the more reserved may prefer a non-committal #96. #111 or #95 doubt the veracity of the Bearer’s statement, while #76 or #168 suggests a teasing doubt and #5 one way of furthering the acquaintance. #124 suggests the meeting has been long overdue, whilst in exceptional circumstances matters may take a romantic or even passionate turn with #196 or #13.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Thanks, but no thanks
body: Whilst recognising the worth of what the Receiver is offering, this Bearer must nevertheless – regretfully or otherwise – decline. Appropriate in response to overtures like #5, #7 and #13 as well as #87 or #89. #188 is frequently useful to Bearers wishing to beat a tactful retreat. Responses can, accordingly, be somewhat negative: a comparatively mild #186 proposes mutual denial; #36 or #144 make resentment at the Bearer’s rejection abundantly clear; while #111 expresses outright disbelief, #127 awkwardness, and #122 or #192 variously cutting dismissals. More positively, however, #159, #161 and #105 indicate the Receiver still doesn’t regret their offer to the Bearer, whatever it may have been, and #137 acknowledges the legitimacy of their reasoning. Should the overture have been romantic, #154 constitutes a civilised suggestion of ongoing friendship, while #87 asserts the willingness to perform whatever is necessary to persuade the Bearer to reconsider: #146 expresses disappointment at such disheartening news.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I see what you did there
body: This Bearer is well aware of whatever the Receiver may be up to. Whilst they may have a certain amount of guarded admiration for their dedication, ingenuity, or sheer chutzpah, they nevertheless feel it important their recognition be considered. Receivers perhaps wishing their machinations had not been uncovered can apologise with #27, proclaim innocence with #163, underline the potential value of their failed venture with #161, or express regret with #149, while those grateful for the acknowledgement can say so with #121, and any feeling such acknowledgement somewhat tardy in arriving can point this out with #124. #186 proposes both parties agree to pretend nothing ever happened – although to what extent such decisions are a solution is a moot point.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Thank God for that
body:
Thus speaks a Bearer profoundly glad that events have transpired as they have. Receivers can concur with #171, ask for explanation with #80, and direct congratulations (ironically or otherwise) to themselves with #162 or the Bearer with #147. #111 disbelievingly rejects such an assessment, while #138 blames the Bearer for whatever has resulted, and #109 or #105 acknowledge that whatever experiences Bearer and Receiver have shared they have at least represented a useful – if steep – learning curve.

#190 is also a useful response, to messages as diverse as the passionately proffered possession of #46, the help offered by #89, and the unequivocal #177 – although it is advisable to use the latter with care.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I promise
body: Few words are more poignantly suggestive of permanence than a promise. This Bearer assures the Receiver they will keep their word, whatever the cost; only the Receiver, however, can decide how much faith to place in such assertions. The doubtful have #54 or #111 with which to make their distrust clear, or #60 to advise playing a long game; more optimistic Receivers, however, can respond lovingly with #34 or #4 or gratefully with #121, and declare intent to demonstrate their gratitude with #87.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: My heart bleeds
body: This Bearer is not, perhaps, quite as devastated by the Receiver’s emotional state as the latter may consider appropriate, and wishes the fact to be made known to them. Whether the Receiver considers the Bearer responsible for their condition or otherwise, #192 makes it clear that the latter has an almost ostentatiously clear conscience. Receivers who feel such implicit criticism unjust can reply dismissively with #122 or in equally sarcastic tones with #84; threaten dire consequences with #205; express the longing for things to be otherwise with #95; or lament changes in their relationship with the Bearer by sending #116 or #118. #30, on the other hand, makes the Receiver’s disapproval of the Bearer and their attitude indisputably clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I think not
body:
This Bearer entertains serious doubts about the feasibility, nay, desirability, of whatever the Receiver has proposed. Whilst there may be a degree of courtesy implicit in its suggested consideration, it is hard not to perceive a somewhat sarcastic edge to such declarations.

Receivers wishing the Bearer to reconsider can plead with them to do so with #168, or suggest their reasoning is somewhat faulty with #111 or an uncomprehending #194. There is wilful magnanimity in #148, a plea for faith in #140, determined patience (threatening or otherwise) in #41, and direct challenge in #30. Meanwhile #36 or #144 make the Receiver’s consequent disenchantment with the Bearer quite clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "My heart bleeds" (5.1)

title: Something I said?
body:
The Bearer is perturbed, or potentially guilty. The Receiver seems disconcertingly different, displeased or distant. While necessarily worried as such, they nevertheless seek to ascertain whether they’re responsible for such inexplicable withdrawal.

For Receivers, a curt #73 or #103 may be the only reply necessary. More generous, if troubled, Receivers can respond with a more explanatory #138, a worrying #127 or #114, or a puzzling but potentially comforting #174. More emotive communication is offered by #78, #145, #146 or #149. A simple #117 offers reassurance, while #99 or #114 somewhat the opposite, although both at least promise explanation of any change in behaviour. #36 or #144, on the other hand, make animosity toward the Bearer abundantly clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
notes: Earlier titles: "I think not" (5.1)

title: I'll make it up to you
body: This Bearer has a guilty conscience. Whatever iniquity they may have committed, they are prepared to make whatever reparation the Receiver feels to be necessary to heal the breach. Should the necessity of doing so be apparent to both parties, #62 concurs wholeheartedly, #80 teasingly demands further details, and a simple #121 offers thanks. To send #182 implies the Bearer had few other options, and #94 accepts only conditionally; #124 suggests such a gesture is long overdue. #188 or #193 decline with potentially dubious grace, and #162, #52 or #61 relish the Bearer’s abasement.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You're cute
body: A lighthearted and cheery compliment, whether intended to remark upon the Receiver’s kitten-like qualities or appreciative of their more sensual nature. Should be parties concerned be relative strangers, #5 offers means of furthering their acquaintance, and #1 or #3 make the mutuality of such feelings apparent. For those somewhat better known to one another, #123, #198, #134 or #171 respond in kind. A flippant #163 or #170 maintains a deliberately humorous tone to the exchange, while #188 offers a firm rebuff and #22, #193 or #111 disclaim the compliment entirely. Should the Bearer’s attentions be unwelcome, #101 or #103 establish this clearly, while #104 or #169 offer variously gentle explanations for the Receiver’s withdrawal.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I've always loved you
body:
Whatever their history has been, the Bearer of #197 wishes to declare that love for the Receiver has lain behind all their actions. Whether sent as an initial confession of desire or as reinforcement of a long-held bond, #197 is often a serious and tender gesture of great importance for the parties concerned.

Should the Bearer’s feelings be mutual, #171 or #134 serve to establish the fact, and #190 suggests the culmination of long-held desires. If togetherness is impossible, #17 laments the situation, whereas #60 implicitly promises future satisfaction. #11 advises the Bearer to take care, while an impulsive #13 or anticipatory #61 speak of further joys to come. If the Bearer’s sentiments are unexpected, #111 makes this clear, whilst for those decidedly unenamoured #192, #101 or #103 make matters quite clear.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You're lovely
body: A gesture of appreciation as appropriate between friends as between lovers, #198 simply indicates that the Bearer genuinely appreciates the Receiver’s good qualities, be that generosity, kindness, loyalty or simply good company. #121 thanks the Bearer, #157 displays enthusiasm, while #171 or #134 respond in kind, and a smug #73, #124 or #162 indicates the Bearer’s appreciation is considered no less than the Receiver’s due. The ends of romance are served with #123, #1 or #34. Receivers wishing to disclaim the compliment can do so cheekily with #163 or mock-seriously with #193 or #38, and those wishing the Bearer to cease and desist can indicate the fact with #101, #103 or even #36.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: You'll pay for that
body: Such a Bearer is displeased, and wishes it to be known they have every intent of exacting revenge at their convenience; wise Receivers may well quake in their boots/trainers/metaphorical hipster footwear at such a missive. A pleading #51 or #87 may pacify, or a defiant #86; #107 offers a challenge, while #163 claims innocence, and #151 indicates a potentially perverse pleasure in such threats. #30 opens hostilities in no uncertain terms; #122 dismisses the threat; #144 expresses shocked anger at the Bearer’s words, while #36 declares the Receiver’s contempt.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Ouch
body: Despite their best efforts, this Bearer feels a twinge at the Receiver’s actions. Not quite a stab in the back, but certainly a twist of the knife. Should this have been unintentional on the Receiver’s part, they can apologise with #27, request forgiveness with #113, or elicit further details with #80, an offhand #194 or a concerned #167. Deliberately hurtful Receivers, however, can display contemptuous dismissal with #122 or #36, and indicate that they consider the Bearer’s feelings to be inappropriate with #103. #171 indicates mutual pain, and #11 indicates future care may be advisable.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Help, I'm trapped in a florist's!
body:
A traumatised cry of despair from a Bearer unaccountably finding themselves trapped in a florist's shop, potentially the victim of triffidesque antics on the part of nearby flora or the malicious intent of their fellow man.

Should the fellow man in question be the Receiver, or should they appreciate the Bearer's plight, they might choose to signal the fact with #131. A cryptic #61 suggests untoward events may be about to unfold; #23 accepts this situation as part of life's rich tapestry, and #132 and #117 offer advice and good wishes for the difficult future suggested by such a situation. #165 dismisses the Bearer's potentially playful tone, #189 asserts awareness of the Bearer's potential humour, and #116 a sententious, melancholic warning of the ephemeral nature of human joys.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Be mine
body:
A touching plea for the Receiver to surrender themselves to the Bearer, body, heart and soul, #208 is not to be sent lightly. Accordingly, it is churlish in the extreme for Receivers to treat such a missive with less than the respect it deserves.

Should they wish to decline the Bearer's request, a Receiver may do so tactfully with #27, #76 or a simple #74, sarcastically with #180, or with a marginally condescending #173. Those desirous of such passionate connection but unable to offer it can say this with a regretful #95 or #17, while #60 suggests only circumstances keep Bearer and Receiver apart. A wry #182 indicates such surrender has already occurred, by choice or otherwise, while #3 issues a direct invitation. Passionate assent can be given with #34, #46, #59, #66 or an understated #170. #103, on the other hand, asserts in no uncertain terms that such a plea was inappropriate.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Where now from here?
body:
Such a Bearer requires elucidation before they can proceed. Either the Receiver's feelings are in doubt, or further advice or information is necessary before a decision can be reached or a plan of action concocted. Particularly if recent contact between Bearer and Receiver has been eventful, #209 offers useful means of providing resolution.

Should romantic matters remain unresolved, #1, #130, #154 or even #34 have the potential to make hitherto unspoken feelings clear. Similarly, #104, #154 and #173 provide clarification, even if not necessarily that which the Bearer might desire. Should the relationship between Bearer and Receiver be in turmoil, #114 proposes crisis talks, #176 admits defeat, #69 wonders whether the end has come and #57 offers reassurance this is not, in fact, the case.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I adore you
body:
This Receiver is not just loved but adored: revered and worshipped, in a slightly fluffy way. To send #210 is to express joy in one's connection with someone, as well as appreciation of their more endearing qualities.

Receivers adoring in their turn can send #34, #130, #197 or #106 to say so. Those wishing to express appreciation if not reciprocation can do so with #123 or #198, or a disingenuous #163, whereas those desiring to disparage the Bearer's sentiments can do so with #186, #184, #104 or a cutting #103.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Long time no see
body:
Whether due to geography or circumstance, Bearer and Receiver have been separated for some time, and the Bearer of #211 wishes to lament the fact. A gesture of remembered affection more than passionately unfulfilled desire, #211 is as appropriate between absent friends as parted lovers.

Receivers feeling themselves responsible for unexpected absence can apologise with #27 or a graver #113, while a mundane #96 suggests the situation is soon to be altered. Receivers regretting their prolonged absence from the Bearer can point this out with #115, or offer support and reassurance with #83 or #117. #118 implies such severance is potentially troubling for both parties, and #69 that it may even spell the cessation of whatever significant connection binds the pair together. #52, #22, or a sarcastic #192, on the other hand, suggest the Receiver remains unconcerned by the parting concerned.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: Farewell
body: Sadly, this Receiver is leaving, whether briefly or for some time, and the Bearer of #212 wishes to mark the fact. Should the Receiver sincerely regret their departure, they can apologise for its impact on the Bearer with #27 or #113; parting lovers can request or offer reassurance with #57, #60, #66 or #69; friends can reassure one another of continued attachment with #55, #83 or #96. Those unmoved by the Bearer's departure can signal this with #122, whilst Receivers generally supportive whatever their personal feelings can demonstrate this by sending #132, #126 or #139. #124, #151, or #162, on the other hand, indicates the Receiver by no means regards the Bearer's absence as an unmitigated tragedy.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I missed you
body: This Bearer has deeply regretted the Receiver's absence, and is unutterably glad it has at last come to an end. Whether the pair's separation has lasted hours or months, the simple honesty and affection of #220 rarely goes amiss. Receivers welcoming the Bearer's sentiment can do so courteously with #121, or apologise for their unfortunate absence with #27 or #113. #169, on the other hand, implies such parting a necessity. #209 suggests Bearer and Receiver must now work out how to move forward together. Lovers can offer reassurance and feeling with #197, while #35, #192 or #54 somewhat uncharitably doubt the Bearer's sincerity.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: The penny drops
body:
Suddenly, all becomes clear. In a moment of revelation, the Bearer has understood the significance of recent events or communications, and wishes the Receiver to recognise that they are now fully cognizant of matters arising.

Should the Receiver be less than certain to what the Bearer is referring, #80 requires further detail. #97 and #209 request advice as to how to proceed with this new knowledge, while #184 advises the Bearer to deal with it in no uncertain terms and #174 suggests apparent revelations are deceptive. Emotional responses can be conveyed with #146 or #145, #147 offers sarcastic appreciation, while a direct #160 suggests the Bearer should feel somewhat less sure of themselves.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout

title: I'll never give you up
body:
This Bearer swears never to relinquish the Receiver, disappoint them, prove elusive or abandon them. Further, they promise never to bring the Receiver to tears, bid them farewell or practise painful deception.

Receivers can offer similar surety with #66 or #46, or express cynicism with #111 or #48. #38 suggests the Receiver feels themselves inadequate for such devotion, while #98 or #103 suggest the Bearer's gesture comes as somewhat of a surprise. For the arch, #189 might prove useful.
source: Cryptofloricon/messages.csv (2013-03-25); text matches April 2013 book layout
